name: Gemini Robotics
desc: Gemini Robotics is a Google DeepMind vision-language-action AI MODEL (not a physical robot) that brings Gemini's multimodal reasoning to robot control, letting robots perceive, reason and act from natural-language instructions. Included here as foundational robotics software.

name: Roadrunner
desc: The RAI Institute Roadrunner (launched March 2026) is a 15 kg bipedal-wheeled robot prototype from Marc Raibert's Robotics and AI Institute. Its symmetrical knee-jointed legs end in wheels, giving multi-modal locomotion - side-by-side and in-line wheel modes plus stepping - so it can roll on flat ground and climb stairs. A single learned control policy handles all modes, deployed zero-shot via sim-to-real transfer. Built as a research platform for agile dynamic mobility, with potential for inspection and warehouse use.

name: Moby
desc: Moby is a general-purpose industrial humanoid from Noble Machines (founded 2024, emerged from stealth March 2026). Designed for hazardous, physically demanding work across construction, manufacturing, logistics and energy, it lifts up to 23 kg (50 lb) and is built to handle stairs, scaffolding, unstable terrain and cluttered spaces. It uses AI-driven whole-body control and autonomy, works alongside crews, and is tele-operable for expert intervention. Noble Machines reported shipping units to a Fortune Global 500 customer within 18 months of launch, with partners including Schaeffler and Solomon.
use_cases: Hazardous industrial work: construction, manufacturing, logistics, energy, mining, semiconductor
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for computer vision and navigation
ai_chip: NVIDIA Jetson Orin (single edge AI computer)
actuator_type: Rugged whole-body design (~200 W average power consumption)

name: RIVR Quadruped
desc: RIVR (formerly Swiss-Mile, an ETH Zurich spin-off) builds a wheel-legged robot with powered wheels on its feet, combining the speed and efficiency of rolling on flat ground with the versatility of legs for curbs and stairs. Designed for last-mile delivery and urban logistics, it can carry parcels door-to-door across mixed terrain.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and perception

name: AEON
desc: AEON is an industrial humanoid robot from Sweden-based Hexagon, developed with NVIDIA and unveiled at Hexagon LIVE 2025 (release early 2026). Standing 165 cm and weighing 60 kg, it uses a hybrid wheeled-foot locomotion rather than pure bipedal walking, moving at up to 8.6 km/h while stable under 15 kg payloads. Its 34 actuated joints enable fluid manipulation; an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin runs motion planning, spatial AI and edge reasoning. AEON integrates Hexagon's metrology-grade sensors and LiDAR for sub-millimetre inspection while in motion, building centimetre-accurate digital twins. Targeted at manufacturing, aerospace, automotive and logistics.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and object recognition

name: Lavo AI

Includes a built-in force/torque sensor for force-controlled tasks.

name: JAKA Ai 5
desc: The JAKA JAKA Ai 5 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (5 kg payload, 954 mm reach) from Shanghai-based JAKA with integrated machine vision, featuring wireless drag-and-drop/graphical programming, collision detection and fenceless operation for pick-and-place, assembly, machine tending and palletizing.

name: JAKA Ai 3
desc: The JAKA JAKA Ai 3 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (3 kg payload, 626 mm reach) from Shanghai-based JAKA with integrated machine vision, featuring wireless drag-and-drop/graphical programming, collision detection and fenceless operation for pick-and-place, assembly, machine tending and palletizing.
cameras: Integrated machine vision camera for visual programming and safety

name: JAKA Zu 5S
desc: Force-sensing variant with built-in industrial force sensor and 954mm working radius. Features three force control solutions: constant force, normal tracking, and speed mode. Tri-co interaction capabilities (coexisting, cooperative, cognitive) for advanced human-robot collaboration.

name: TracePen
desc: The Wandelbots TracePen is a handheld teaching device (a stylus-like tool) that lets operators program industrial robots by demonstration - tracing a path in physical space rather than coding - to dramatically speed up robot setup. An accessory/teaching tool rather than a robot itself.

name: Wandelbots NOVA Cloud
desc: Wandelbots NOVA Cloud is the cloud edition of Wandelbots' robot-agnostic operating system (software, not a robot), letting developers program and orchestrate industrial robots from multiple makers through a unified cloud API.
cameras: Supports integration with various camera systems for visual monitoring

name: Grav Enhanced Gripper
desc: Flexiv's Grav Enhanced Gripper is an enhanced gripper/end-effector in the Grav line for adaptive grasping. (An end-effector; specifications worth verifying.)

name: Grav
desc: Flexiv's Grav is part of the company's adaptive-robotics portfolio emphasising force-aware manipulation. (Detailed payload/reach specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against Flexiv.)

name: Rizon 10s
desc: Flexiv's Rizon 10s is a higher-payload (~10 kg class) 7-axis adaptive robot with the company's signature force-control technology for robust contact-rich manipulation such as grinding, polishing and assembly.
cameras: Built-in vision system with depth perception

name: Rizon 4s
desc: Flexiv's Rizon 4s is a 7-axis adaptive robot (~4 kg payload class) built around industry-leading force-torque sensing and hierarchical force control, excelling at contact-rich tasks like polishing, assembly and surface finishing.

name: JAKA Lumi
desc: JAKA Lumi is a lightweight collaborative robot arm from JAKA, designed for easy deployment in collaborative automation, light assembly and education. (Detailed payload/reach specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against JAKA.)

name: JAKA Ai Series (Ai 3/5/7/12/18)
desc: The JAKA Ai (All-in-one) Series spans five 6-axis cobots - Ai 3, 5, 7, 12 and 18 (3-18 kg payload, 626-1327 mm reach) - each with integrated plug-and-play machine vision, wireless teaching and graphical programming, built on JAKA's S3 (Smart, Simple, Small) design principles.
cameras: Integrated machine vision cameras for visual protection and guidance

name: JAKA Ai 7
desc: The JAKA JAKA Ai 7 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (7 kg payload, 796 mm reach) from Shanghai-based JAKA with integrated machine vision, featuring wireless drag-and-drop/graphical programming, collision detection and fenceless operation for pick-and-place, assembly, machine tending and palletizing.

name: AUBO iV-Vision Series
desc: The AUBO iV-Vision Series integrates machine vision with AUBO's cobots for vision-guided picking, inspection and adaptive automation. (A vision system/series rather than a single arm.)
cameras: Integrated industrial camera with adjustable light source

name: AUBO-iS35
desc: The AUBO-iS35 is a high-payload 35 kg 6-axis cobot for heavy palletizing and machine tending.

name: AUBO-iS20L
desc: The AUBO-iS20L is a long-reach 20 kg-payload 6-axis cobot in AUBO's iS series for palletizing and large-workspace handling.

name: AUBO i20
desc: The AUBO i20 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (20 kg payload) from AUBO Robotics, offering drag-teach programming and fenceless operation for machine tending, assembly and material handling.

name: AUBO i16
desc: The AUBO i16 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (16 kg payload) from AUBO Robotics, offering drag-teach programming and fenceless operation for machine tending, assembly and material handling.

safety_features: Collision detection, force limiting, safety-rated monitored stop

name: AUBO i10
desc: The AUBO i10 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (10 kg payload) from AUBO Robotics, offering drag-teach programming and fenceless operation for machine tending, assembly and material handling.

name: AUBO i7
desc: Mid-range cobot with 786.5mm reach, ±0.02mm repeatability, 24kg weight. Launched across APAC markets for diverse industrial applications.
safety_features: Collision detection, force limiting, emergency stop

name: AUBO i5
desc: Versatile cobot with 886.5mm reach, ±0.02-0.05mm repeatability, 24kg weight. Compact design with open system platform for flexible integration. Perfect for machine operating tasks and assembly applications.

name: AUBO i3
desc: Compact lightweight cobot with 625mm reach, ±0.02-0.05mm repeatability, 16kg weight. Ideal for tight clearances, light assembly, and repeated movement applications. Features open SDK supporting C, C++, C#, Lua, and Python.

name: AGV+COBOT Integrated Solution
desc: Hanwha's AGV+COBOT Integrated Solution combines an autonomous mobile robot with an HCR collaborative arm for mobile manipulation - autonomously navigating a facility to tend machines and move parts.
cameras: Integrated Hanwha Techwin camera technology for Robot Monitoring Service (RMS)

name: HCR Advanced Series (Extended Range)
desc: Hanwha's HCR Advanced Series (Extended Range) extends the HCR cobot family with longer reach for larger work envelopes such as palletizing and multi-machine tending.
safety_features: Collision detection, Force limiting, Emergency stop

name: Sterimove
desc: Billed as the world's first mobile robot compatible with GMP cleanroom Grades A/B/C/D, designed for pharmaceutical sterile-production environments where conventional AGVs cannot operate.
highlights: First mobile robot for GMP Grade A/B/C/D

name: FL1500
desc: Ultra-compact 1.5-tonne counterbalanced forklift AGV with a modular counterbalance-weight and battery design. Equipped with a hydraulic mono mast, it moves, stacks and rack-stores pallets and containers, and is highly maneuverable with a small turning circle.
cameras: 3D vision system for navigation and obstacle detection

name: TS2-100
desc: The Staubli TS2-100 is a 4-axis SCARA robot (8.4 kg payload, 1000 mm reach) with proprietary JCS drives for ultra-short cycle times, repeatability to +/-0.01 mm and a fully encapsulated IP65 hygienic design.

name: TS2-80
desc: The Staubli TS2-80 is a 4-axis SCARA robot (8.4 kg payload, 800 mm reach) with proprietary JCS drives for ultra-short cycle times, repeatability to +/-0.01 mm and a fully encapsulated IP65 hygienic design.

name: TS2-60
desc: The Staubli TS2-60 is a 4-axis SCARA robot (8.4 kg payload, 620 mm reach) with proprietary JCS drives for ultra-short cycle times, repeatability to +/-0.01 mm and a fully encapsulated IP65 hygienic design.

name: TS2-40
desc: The Staubli TS2-40 is a 4-axis SCARA robot (4 kg payload, 400 mm reach) with proprietary JCS drives for ultra-short cycle times, repeatability to +/-0.01 mm and a fully encapsulated IP65 hygienic design.

name: TX2-200L
desc: The Staubli TX2-200L is a fast, rigid 6-axis industrial robot (90 kg payload, 2609 mm reach) from Switzerland, known for high path accuracy and hygienic/cleanroom variants, with optional SIL3-PLe safety for human collaboration.

desc: The Staubli TX2-60 is a fast, rigid 6-axis industrial robot (9 kg payload, 670 mm reach) from Switzerland, known for high path accuracy and hygienic/cleanroom variants, with optional SIL3-PLe safety for human collaboration.

name: CarryPick KMP600
desc: Swisslog's CarryPick (KMP600) is an autonomous mobile robot that lifts and transports mobile storage racks to picking stations in a goods-to-person fulfillment system, carrying up to ~600 kg.

name: Relay (ASR-200)
desc: The Relay ASR-200 (Autonomous Service Robot, originally from Savioke) is a compact indoor delivery robot for hotels, hospitals and offices, autonomously navigating corridors and operating elevators to deliver amenities, supplies and small items to rooms and departments.

name: Robot Visual Safety (RVS)
desc: Hanwha's Robot Visual Safety (RVS) is a camera-based safety system that monitors the area around a cobot for speed-and-separation safety - a safety subsystem rather than a robot.
cameras: Dual 3D cameras for depth perception and human detection

name: Robot AI 3D Vision (RAIV)
desc: Hanwha's Robot AI 3D Vision (RAIV) is a 3D machine-vision system that gives Hanwha cobots AI-driven object recognition and bin-picking - a perception add-on rather than a standalone robot.
cameras: 3D stereo camera with depth sensing capability
ai_model: Deep learning neural network for object recognition

name: HCR-10L
desc: The Hanwha HCR-10L is a 6-axis collaborative robot (10 kg payload) with a slim design and intuitive direct-teaching for fenceless machine tending, assembly and palletizing.

name: HCR-14
desc: The Hanwha HCR-14 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (14 kg payload) with a slim design and intuitive direct-teaching for fenceless machine tending, assembly and palletizing.

desc: The Hanwha HCR-12A is a 6-axis collaborative robot (12 kg payload) with a slim design and intuitive direct-teaching for fenceless machine tending, assembly and palletizing.

desc: The Hanwha HCR-5A is a 6-axis collaborative robot (5 kg payload) with a slim design and intuitive direct-teaching for fenceless machine tending, assembly and palletizing.

name: HCR-3A
desc: The Hanwha HCR-3A is a 6-axis collaborative robot (3 kg payload) with a slim design and intuitive direct-teaching for fenceless machine tending, assembly and palletizing.

name: Hospital AGV (Fork)
desc: Fork-type hospital AGV configuration in the TransCar family, able to pick up and handle a wide range of trolleys for food, waste, pharmaceuticals and non-standard loads. Part of the OTSAW–Swisslog Healthcare hospital logistics system with elevator and door integration for autonomous multi-floor delivery.
highlights: Part of the TransCar hospital AGV system

name: Hospital AGV (Tower)
desc: Tower-type hospital AGV configuration in the TransCar family for vertical transport tasks, designed for intensive clinical use with natural-feature navigation. Integrates with elevators and doors for autonomous multi-floor material movement within healthcare facilities.
highlights: Part of the TransCar hospital AGV system
cameras: 3D vision cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: Hospital AGV (Platform)
desc: Platform-type hospital AGV configuration in the TransCar family for transporting patient meals, linens, trash and medical waste. Uses natural-feature laser navigation and integrates with the hospital's elevators and doors for autonomous in-house delivery.
highlights: Part of the TransCar hospital AGV system

name: Relay ASR-200
desc: The healthcare configuration of the Relay ASR-200 autonomous service robot, deployed in hospitals to deliver medications, specimens and supplies between departments, navigating autonomously and using elevators for secure point-to-point delivery.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: TransCar AGV
desc: The TransCar AGV (Swisslog, with OTSAW) is an automated guided vehicle for heavy hospital logistics - autonomously transporting carts of meals, linen, sterile supplies and waste through corridors and elevators, handling the high-volume material flows of large hospitals.
cameras: Multiple safety cameras and navigation cameras

name: Relay
desc: The Relay robot (originally from Savioke, deployed in healthcare via Swisslog) is a compact autonomous delivery robot that carries medications, specimens and small items through hospitals, navigating autonomously and operating elevators for secure point-to-point delivery.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: TUG T4
desc: Industrial open-platform variant of the TUG from ST Engineering Aethon, built for manufacturing and warehouse material flow. An independent suspension system handles uneven floors, with roughly 5° slope capability and a tight ~17-inch turning radius. The open deck integrates with active payloads and conveyors.
cameras: Multiple safety cameras and navigation sensors

name: TUG T2
desc: Autonomous cabinet robot from ST Engineering Aethon for secure delivery of medications and specimens in hospitals. Lockable drawers (11-drawer, 9-drawer 2× deep, 7-drawer 4× deep, or door-cart configurations) open via combined PIN code and fingerprint biometric access. Navigates with overlapping laser, sonar and infrared sensors — no wires or magnets — and integrates with elevators and doors over WiFi.
highlights: WiFi link to Aethon Command Center
cameras: Multiple stereo cameras for navigation and obstacle detection
api: Encrypted VPN to Aethon Command Center

name: TUG T3
desc: Autonomous mobile robot from ST Engineering Aethon that tows carts and racks for hospital and industrial material transport — meals, linens, waste and supplies. Omnidirectional four-wheel drive with 2D SLAM and multi-sensor (LiDAR, sonar, infrared) navigation; auto-docks and auto-charges for near-24/7 operation and integrates with elevators, doors and fire systems over WiFi. Deployed across 250+ hospitals.
api: Encrypted VPN to Aethon Command Center

name: RoboCourier
desc: Swisslog Healthcare's RoboCourier is an autonomous mobile robot for hospital logistics, navigating corridors and using elevators to deliver medications, lab specimens and supplies between departments, freeing clinical staff from courier runs.
cameras: Multiple stereo cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: ItemPiQ
desc: Swisslog's ItemPiQ is a robotic piece-picking cell - a vision-guided robotic arm that picks individual items for order fulfillment in automated warehouses.
cameras: 3D vision system with smart image recognition

name: IntraMove AMR 3000
desc: AI-driven horizontal pallet-transport AMR rated for 3000 kg. Navigates by SLAM using two laser scanners with AI path planning — no cables, strips or tape — and carries an integrated lifting device with interchangeable top modules (platforms, conveyors). Connects to fleet management via the VDA 5050 standard and links to Swisslog's SynQ WMS/WCS. Heavy-duty omnidirectional drive enables sideways movement.
cameras: Multiple safety cameras and navigation sensors
api: VDA 5050; MQTT / ModBus / OPC UA for peripherals

name: IntraMove AMR 1500
desc: AI-driven horizontal pallet-transport AMR rated for 1500 kg. Navigates by SLAM using two laser scanners with AI path planning — no cables, strips or tape — and carries an integrated lifting device with interchangeable top modules (platforms, conveyors). Connects to fleet management via the VDA 5050 standard and links to Swisslog's SynQ WMS/WCS.
cameras: Multiple safety cameras and navigation cameras
api: VDA 5050; MQTT / ModBus / OPC UA for peripherals

name: IntraMove AMR 600
desc: AI-driven horizontal pallet-transport AMR rated for 600 kg. Navigates by SLAM using two laser scanners with AI path planning — no cables, strips or tape — and carries an integrated lifting device with interchangeable top modules (platforms, conveyors). Connects to fleet management via the VDA 5050 standard and links to Swisslog's SynQ WMS/WCS.
api: VDA 5050; MQTT / ModBus / OPC UA for peripherals

name: R5 (Red Line)
desc: Fifth-generation Red Line grid robot that drives across the top of an aluminum cube-storage grid, digging out and delivering bins to workstations for goods-to-person fulfillment. Eight wheels enable five-directional movement; each robot is independently controlled with no single point of failure.

name: Galbot Humanoid Robot
desc: Galbot (Galaxy General, Beijing) builds a wheeled humanoid that pairs dual dexterous arms with a wheeled mobile base and a telescoping torso for stable mobile manipulation. Trained using NVIDIA Isaac Sim and the DexGraspNet dataset, it targets retail, service and unmanned-store applications.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for vision and navigation

name: Galbot G1 Wheeled Bionic Robot
desc: The Galbot G1 is Galaxy General's wheeled 'bionic' humanoid - dual dexterous arms on a wheeled base with a telescoping torso for stable mobile manipulation, targeted at unmanned retail and pharmacy fulfillment.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth cameras for navigation and manipulation

name: Galbot S1
desc: The Galbot S1 is a configuration of Galaxy General's wheeled humanoid, combining dexterous dual arms with a mobile base for mobile manipulation in retail and service environments such as unmanned stores and pharmacies.

name: MenteeBot
desc: Mentee Robotics' MenteeBot is an AI-centric general-purpose humanoid (~175 cm) built end-to-end around learning - combining simulation-to-real training, natural-language task understanding, navigation and manipulation. Founded by AI and robotics academics, Mentee positions MenteeBot for home and warehouse tasks driven by an integrated AI brain.

name: MenteeBot V3.1
desc: MenteeBot V3.1 is a further iteration of Mentee Robotics' AI humanoid, refining the V3 platform's perception, locomotion and language-driven manipulation for general-purpose home and warehouse work.

name: MenteeBot V3.0
desc: MenteeBot V3.0 is an iteration of Mentee Robotics' AI-driven general-purpose humanoid, advancing its end-to-end learning stack for locomotion, natural-language task planning and manipulation in home and warehouse settings.

name: MenteeBot V3.0/V3.1
desc: A combined record for Mentee Robotics' MenteeBot V3.0/V3.1 AI humanoid generations (~175 cm), built end-to-end around learning for navigation, language understanding and manipulation. (Appears to duplicate the separate V3.0 and V3.1 records.)
use_cases: Warehouse & household tasks via natural-language commands

name: HUBO
desc: HUBO is the pioneering Korean research humanoid developed at KAIST and commercialised by Rainbow Robotics - a full bipedal platform (~125 cm) that became the basis for the DRC-HUBO that won the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge. Widely used for humanoid locomotion and manipulation research.

name: Clone Torso
desc: Clone Torso is Clone Robotics' upper-body musculoskeletal demonstrator - a synthetic skeleton with Myofiber artificial muscles showcasing human-like dexterity in the arms, wrists and hands, a stepping stone toward the full-body Protoclone/Clone Alpha android.

name: Clone Alpha Android
desc: Clone Alpha is Clone Robotics' musculoskeletal home android (a limited run of 279), driven by water-actuated Myofiber artificial muscles on a synthetic human skeleton. (Record of the Clone Alpha android - see also the Protoclone development record.)

name: Neoclone
desc: NeoClone is part of Clone Robotics' biomimetic android work using the company's Myofiber water-actuated artificial-muscle technology. (Detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against Clone Robotics.)
cameras: Multiple high-resolution cameras for vision and facial recognition

name: Protoclone V1
desc: Clone Robotics' Protoclone V1 (2025) is billed as the world's first bipedal musculoskeletal android - a polymer skeleton replicating ~206 human bones, actuated by 1,000+ water-driven 'Myofiber' artificial muscles (under-50ms response, >30% contraction), with 200+ degrees of freedom, 500+ sensors, a 500 W pump 'heart' and an NVIDIA Jetson Thor in the skull running Clone's Cybernet model.
cameras: Multiple cameras for vision and navigation

name: Clone Hand
desc: The Clone Hand is Clone Robotics' biomimetic robotic hand actuated by water-driven Myofiber artificial muscles on an anatomically accurate skeleton, reproducing human-like finger dexterity for its androids and research.

name: Clone Alpha
desc: Clone Alpha is the productized version of Clone Robotics' Protoclone musculoskeletal android, planned as a limited run of 279 units. It uses the same water-actuated Myofiber artificial muscles on an anatomically accurate skeleton for lifelike, human-like motion in a featherweight home android.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for vision and navigation

name: HUBO-2 Plus
desc: HUBO-2 Plus is an upgraded version of Rainbow Robotics' HUBO-2 research humanoid, with refinements to the actuators and control for more robust bipedal research and demonstration.

name: RB-Y1 Bimanual Mobile Manipulator
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 bimanual mobile manipulator combines two cobot arms on a wheeled, liftable base for two-handed mobile manipulation. (Record of the RB-Y1 mobile manipulator.)
cameras: RGB-D cameras for perception and navigation

name: Milk Tea Barista Robot
desc: A Rainbow Robotics robotic barista system for automated milk/bubble-tea preparation, using collaborative arms to dispense, mix and serve drinks in unattended cafe and kiosk settings. (Duplicate-style record of Rainbow's barista product.)
cameras: Multiple cameras for object recognition and customer interaction

name: FX-2
desc: The HUBO FX-2 is part of Rainbow Robotics' FX series of large bipedal robots - successors to the FX-1, a rideable two-legged platform able to carry a human passenger and walk. A demonstration of large-scale bipedal locomotion and load-bearing. (Detailed specifications worth verifying.)

name: HUBO2
desc: HUBO2 is a record of the KAIST/Rainbow Robotics second-generation research humanoid (~125 cm, ~45 kg), a platform for bipedal locomotion and manipulation research. (Appears to duplicate the HUBO-2 record.)
cameras: Color cameras in head for vision processing

name: ROBAN
desc: The Leju ROBAN is a 22-DOF medium-size bipedal humanoid for advanced education and research, featuring Leju's self-stabilising gait algorithms and torque servos. Programmable in Python with onboard vision, it is used in universities and competitions such as RoboCup to study humanoid locomotion, manipulation and AI.

name: KUAVO 3.0
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo 3.0 is a generation of the full-size Kuavo humanoid (360 N.m joints, ~4.6 km/h omnidirectional gait, KaihongOS) with refinements in motion and AI for service, education and research deployments.

name: RB Serving Robot
desc: Autonomous serving robot from Rainbow Robotics (a KAIST humanoid-lab spin-out) that uses the company's patented grid-free SLAM to localize and navigate without floor markers, carrying food and items to tables in restaurants and hospitality settings.

name: ASTRO
desc: A Rainbow Robotics platform - from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, RB-series cobots and quadrupeds. (Detailed specifications for this specific record are limited and worth verifying against Rainbow Robotics.)

name: DRC-HUBO
desc: DRC-HUBO, from KAIST and Rainbow Robotics, is the humanoid that won the DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals in 2015. Its standout trick is transforming between walking on two legs and kneeling onto wheels in its knees to roll quickly and stably, letting it drive a vehicle, open doors, turn valves, cut walls and traverse rubble - the full DRC task list - more reliably than rivals.
cameras: Stereo vision cameras and additional sensors for navigation
robot_form: Transformable humanoid (walks; kneels onto knee wheels)

name: HUBO-2
desc: HUBO-2 is the second-generation KAIST/Rainbow Robotics research humanoid (~125 cm, ~45 kg, ~40 DOF), improving on the original HUBO's walking and manipulation as a platform for academic humanoid research.

name: RB-Y1
desc: Rainbow Robotics' RB-Y1 is a bimanual mobile manipulator - two collaborative arms on a wheeled, height-adjustable mobile base - for dynamic dual-arm tasks in service, logistics and research.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth cameras for perception

name: RB20-1900
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB20-1900 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (20 kg payload, 1900 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.

name: RB16-900
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB16-900 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (16 kg payload, 900 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.

name: RB10-1300
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB10-1300 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (10 kg payload, 1300 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.

name: RB5-850
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB5-850 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (5 kg payload, 850 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.
cameras: Built-in vision system with RGB camera

name: RB3-1200
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB3-1200 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (3 kg payload, 1200 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.

name: RB3-730
desc: The Rainbow Robotics RB3-730 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (3 kg payload, 730 mm reach) from the Korean maker of the HUBO humanoid, with in-house actuators and an intuitive teaching interface for fenceless automation.

name: AELOS 1s
desc: The Leju AELOS 1S is an entry model in the AELOS educational-humanoid line, using graphical block programming and an app to teach coding and robotics through walking, dancing and preset motion routines aimed at younger students.

name: PANDO
desc: The Leju PANDO is a miniature humanoid robot (introduced 2018) positioned as an entry-level product for younger students entering the AELOS/Leju education line. Compact and app-controlled with block programming, it focuses on introductory robotics, coding and interactive play.

name: KUAVO 5-W
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo 5-W is a wheeled-base configuration of the Kuavo 5 humanoid, trading bipedal legs for a mobile wheeled base for stable, long-duty service mobility while keeping the dual-arm upper body and KaihongOS intelligence.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth cameras

name: KUAVO 5
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo 5 is a newer generation of the Kuavo full-size humanoid (high-torque joints, omnidirectional walking, KaihongOS with large-model AI) for service, education and embodied-AI research.
cameras: RGB-D cameras for perception and navigation
ai_model: Custom AI framework with computer vision and motion planning

name: AELOS PRO
desc: The Leju AELOS Pro is a 19-degree-of-freedom educational humanoid robot with high-precision servos for lifelike walking, dancing and martial-arts moves. A built-in HD camera enables facial recognition and object tracking, 14+ sensor ports allow custom builds, and it programs via Blockly drag-and-drop or Python - bridging beginner to advanced STEM and competition robotics.

name: AELOS LITE
desc: The Leju AELOS Lite is a 17-DOF programmable humanoid built for classroom STEM learning - it walks, dances, boxes and plays soccer, with a head that rotates ~160 degrees. Block-based Scratch/Blockly programming makes it approachable for beginners, and its torque-composite servos give long life and precise motion.

name: KUAVO 4Pro
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo 4 Pro is an upgraded generation of the Kuavo full-size humanoid, building on the 360 N.m-joint, KaihongOS platform with improved performance for commercial service and research.
cameras: RGB-D cameras and stereo vision system
ai_model: Custom neural networks for perception and navigation

name: KUAVO 5/5-W
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo 5.5-W is a wheeled variant in the Kuavo 5 series, pairing the dual-arm humanoid upper body with a wheeled base for service and mobile-manipulation tasks.

name: KUAVO-MY
desc: Leju Robotics' Kuavo MY is a configuration of the Kuavo full-size humanoid platform (360 N.m joints, KaihongOS). (Detailed variant specifications are limited and worth verifying against Leju.)
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and interaction

name: OmniHand Pro 2025
desc: The AGIBOT OmniHand Pro (2025) is the high-end dexterous hand in AGIBOT's OmniHand line, adding more articulation and richer tactile sensing for fine, human-like manipulation.

name: OmniHand 2025
desc: The AGIBOT OmniHand (2025) is a dexterous multi-finger robotic hand with tactile feedback for human-like grasping, used as an end-effector on AGIBOT's humanoid robots.
cameras: Integrated tactile sensing array with force and pressure sensors

name: C5
desc: The C5 is a robot vacuum from AGIBOT that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.
cameras: Visual navigation cameras for SLAM positioning
use_cases: Commercial floor cleaning: sweep, scrub, mop with auto-charge, self-filling water tank & self-cleaning drainage

name: D1 Pro
desc: AGIBOT's D1 Pro is a compact industrial quadruped with 12 degrees of freedom, ~3.7 m/s top speed and an 8 kg payload, using reinforcement-learning gait control for dynamic locomotion across varied terrain. A flexible base for inspection, demonstration and light mobile-robotics projects.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and perception

name: D1 Ultra
desc: AGIBOT's D1 Ultra is a rugged industrial quadruped with RL-based all-terrain gait control: ~3.7 m/s, a 35 cm jump, 30-degree slope climbing, 16 cm stair steps and IP54 protection, with ~48 N·m peak joint torque. Open-SDK and payload-ready (LiDAR, depth cameras, 4G/5G) for security inspection and emergency response.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and perception
use_cases: Industrial quadruped: security patrol, emergency response, inspection (35 cm jump, all-terrain RL gait)

name: G2
desc: AGIBOT's G2 is an industrial wheeled humanoid introduced in 2025 for mobile manipulation and logistics, pairing a humanoid upper body with a wheeled base for stable, long-duty operation in commercial and industrial settings.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for vision and navigation
actuator_type: Wheeled humanoid, dual arms (sub-millimetre operation precision)

name: G1
desc: An AGIBOT research/development platform from the Shanghai-based embodied-AI company behind the open-source Lingxi X1 humanoid and the A2 service humanoid. (Detailed specifications for this specific record are limited and worth verifying against AGIBOT.)
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and object recognition

name: X2 Ultra
desc: AGIBOT's Lingxi X2 Ultra is the sensor-rich, developer-enabled member of the compact X2 series (~1.31 m, ~39 kg), adding a richer perception suite for research and perception-heavy service while retaining the agile half-size form.
cameras: RGB-D cameras for computer vision and facial recognition

name: X2
desc: AGIBOT's Lingxi X2 is a compact half-size humanoid (~1.31 m, ~35 kg, ~27-31 DOF) built for education, research, entertainment and service. Agile enough to walk, run, dance and ride a bicycle, it uses the AimDK_X2 developer kit with AGIBOT's WorkGPT AI and GO-1 foundation model.
cameras: RGB camera with computer vision capabilities
use_cases: Compact interactive humanoid (rides bicycles, scooters, hoverboards)
cpu: Xyber-Edge cerebellar controller + DCU decision unit

name: X1
desc: The AGIBOT X1 (Lingxi X1) is a fully open-source modular humanoid robot: 130 cm, 33 kg, 34 degrees of freedom on PowerFlow quasi-direct-drive servos (R86-3 actuator up to 200 N.m peak), walking at ~1 m/s with a 2-hour runtime. Built on the AimRT framework with reinforcement-learning locomotion and free design/software access, it is a benchtop-friendly platform for research and maker communities.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth cameras
sdk: Fully open-source: design materials, software frameworks, AimRT middleware & motion-control source

name: A2-W
desc: AGIBOT's A2-W is the wheeled, dual-arm version of the Yuanzheng A2, mounting the humanoid upper body on a 4WD mobile base with hot-swappable batteries for stable, long-duty mobile manipulation in service and logistics.

name: A2 Lite
desc: AGIBOT's A2 Lite is the cost-efficient service member of the full-size Yuanzheng A2 family, with 23 DOF, a simplified hand and Wi-Fi interaction but no LiDAR/RGB-D, aimed at affordable human-robot-interaction roles such as reception, guidance and exhibition presentations.

name: Kepler Forerunner D1
desc: Kepler's Forerunner D1 is a variant in the Shanghai Kepler Forerunner humanoid family. (Detailed specifications for this variant are limited and worth verifying against Kepler.)
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for vision and navigation

name: Ameca Generation 3
desc: Engineered Arts' Ameca Generation 3 is the latest of the world's most advanced expressive humanoid for human-robot interaction - its grey, deliberately non-human face uses Mesmer technology for remarkably lifelike micro-expressions and gestures, with integrated conversational AI (LLM-driven) for natural dialogue. Used widely for research, exhibitions and AI demonstrations.

name: Forerunner S1
desc: Kepler's Forerunner S1 is a variant in the Shanghai Kepler full-size humanoid family aimed at commercial and industrial deployment. (Detailed specifications for this variant are limited and worth verifying against Kepler.)

name: Quinn
desc: Quinn is an Engineered Arts humanoid robot from the UK maker of RoboThespian, Mesmer and Ameca, focused on lifelike expression and human-robot interaction for displays, research and education. (Detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against Engineered Arts.)
cameras: Multiple HD cameras for facial recognition and interaction

name: Ami and Azi Desktop
desc: Ami and Azi are Engineered Arts' desktop interactive robots - expressive tabletop heads designed for conversation and engagement, showcasing the company's facial animation and HRI software in a compact pair of units.

name: RoboThespian
desc: Engineered Arts' RoboThespian is a life-size interactive humanoid robot built for visitor attractions, science centres and education. Highly expressive through gestures, speech and projected facial animation, and remotely operable for telepresence, it has been one of the most widely deployed entertainment/education humanoids worldwide.

name: Mesmer
desc: Mesmer is Engineered Arts' technology and product line for hyper-realistic human-like androids - lifelike silicone skin, detailed faces and smooth actuation, designed to look convincingly human (unlike the deliberately robotic Ameca) for attractions, telepresence and entertainment.

name: Ameca Desktop
desc: The Ameca Desktop is a head-and-torso tabletop version of Engineered Arts' Ameca humanoid, delivering the same expressive face, gestures and conversational AI in a compact, fixed form factor for desktop interaction, demos and reception.
cameras: Multiple cameras for facial tracking and expression mapping

name: Ami
desc: Ami is a desktop interactive robot from Engineered Arts - a smaller expressive head/face platform built for natural conversation and engagement, bringing the company's HRI and animation technology to an accessible tabletop unit.

name: Type-X RCV
desc: Milrem's Type-X is a 12-tonne tracked robotic combat vehicle (RCV) that can mount up to a 50 mm autocannon plus a 7.62 mm machine gun, with STANAG 4569 Level 4 armour. Hybrid-electric and capable of 80 km/h, it is designed to fight alongside crewed armour as an expendable wingman carrying ~4.1 tonnes of payload.
cameras: Multiple electro-optical and thermal imaging cameras

name: THeMIS Support
desc: The THeMIS Support configuration adapts Milrem's tracked UGV for combat-support roles - mounting remote weapon stations, ISR sensors or mission payloads on the modular 1,200 kg platform to extend infantry capability while keeping soldiers at a safer standoff.
cameras: Multiple day/night cameras with thermal imaging

name: THeMIS Cargo
desc: The THeMIS Cargo is the logistics/CASEVAC configuration of Milrem's tracked UGV, carrying supplies, ammunition or wounded personnel up to 1,200 kg. A THeMIS in this role was the first UGV in service with the Ukrainian Armed Forces, deployed from August 2022.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and situational awareness

name: ARCOS
desc: ARCOS is part of Milrem's intelligent-functions/autonomy offering, providing autonomous navigation and behaviours for its UGV and RCV platforms. (System-level offering - detailed specifications limited.)
cameras: Multiple camera feeds from connected UGVs

name: MRCV
desc: The MRCV (Milrem Robotic Combat Vehicle) is Milrem's robotic combat vehicle developed within the European iMUGS (integrated Modular Unmanned Ground System) programme, advancing standardised, interoperable robotic combat capability across EU armies.

name: VECTOR RCV
desc: The Vector is the tracked counterpart to Milrem's HAVOC RCV, in development to share the company's unified autonomy ecosystem and hybrid-electric driveline while offering tracked mobility better suited to soft or northern-European terrain. (Concept/development stage - specifications to be confirmed.)
cameras: Multiple electro-optical cameras and thermal imaging systems

name: HAVOC 8x8 RCV
desc: Milrem's HAVOC is an 8x8 wheeled robotic combat vehicle (unveiled 2025) weighing ~15 tonnes with a 5-tonne payload. Its hybrid-electric driveline (near-silent, instant torque) delivers 110 km/h on road and 600 km range, with AI-driven navigation and electronic-warfare resilience, designed to support armoured formations and mount weapons up to 30 mm.
cameras: Multi-spectral sensor suite with thermal and night vision capabilities

name: THeMIS
desc: Milrem's THeMIS (Tracked Hybrid Modular Infantry System) is the world's most widely fielded tracked UGV - part of robotic programmes in 19 countries. A 1.63-tonne hybrid-electric platform carrying up to 1,200 kg, it supports infantry across Logistics, Combat, ISR and EOD configurations, climbs 60% slopes and has been combat-proven in Ukraine since 2022.

name: Multiscope
desc: MultiScope is a THeMIS-based multi-mission family from Milrem, configurable for tasks such as route clearance/demining, ISR and logistics by swapping mission modules onto the tracked 1,200 kg platform.
cameras: Multiple camera systems for navigation and surveillance

name: Carbon ATK (AutoTractor Kit)
desc: Retrofittable autonomy kit that transforms conventional tractors into driverless machines, monitored 24/7 in real time by trained Carbon Robotics operators at the Remote Operations Control Center (ROCC). Initially compatible with John Deere 6R and 8R Series tractors, installable in under 24 hours without permanent modifications. Performs LaserWeeder operations plus ground prep (tilling, plowing, cultivating, ripping, discing, listing, mulching, mowing). Pay-per-hour pricing model with no upfront purchase. Originally launched as 'Carbon AutoTractor', rebranded to 'Carbon ATK' in late 2025.
autonomy_level: Full autonomy with remote human supervision
remote_supervision_detail: 24/7 monitoring at Remote Operations Control Center (ROCC), Richland WA. Operators can take over remotely for obstacles (debris, wildlife, irrigation pipes)

name: LaserWeeder G2 1800
desc: Largest LaserWeeder G2 model at 60 ft (18.3 m) wide, weighing 14,000 lbs (6,350 kg). Built for large-scale organic corn and soybean operations on farms standardized on 60-foot-wide farming equipment (common in the US Midwest). Same Carbon AI + 240W diode laser technology as the rest of the G2 family but at maximum throughput — 5-10 acres per hour of weed control without herbicides, mechanical cultivation, or soil disturbance.

name: LaserWeeder G2 1200
desc: First broadacre laser weeding solution from Carbon Robotics, specifically designed for organic corn and soybean operations. At 40 ft (12.2 m) wide and 12,000 lbs (5,443 kg) with 48x 240W diode lasers and corresponding camera/LED arrays, it's the first weed control system that doesn't disturb crops or soil — a key advantage in row crop farming where mechanical cultivation damages plants and tillage disrupts soil health. Particularly impactful for organic corn/soy producers.
use_cases: Row crop weed control without tillage

name: LaserWeeder G2 600
desc: Flagship LaserWeeder G2 model — the next generation of Carbon Robotics' industry-leading 20-foot laser weeder. 25% lighter than the original LaserWeeder (Gen 1) at 7,200 lbs / 3,266 kg with 24x 240W diode lasers, 36 cameras, and 240 LED bedtop lights. Twice the throughput of Gen 1, sub-millimeter accuracy, and 99% weed kill rate. Designed for the wide range of specialty vegetable and herb crops where Carbon Robotics has its largest installed customer base.

name: LaserWeeder G2 400
desc: Mid-sized LaserWeeder G2 model designed for diverse crop types and field layouts. At 13.3 ft (4.0 m) wide with 16x 240W diode lasers, 24 cameras, and 160 LED bedtop lights, it's the versatile workhorse of the G2 line. Sub-millimeter weed targeting accuracy with 5,000+ weeds shot per minute and up to 99% kill rate. Pairs with mid-size row crop tractors.

name: LaserWeeder G2 300
desc: Six-module LaserWeeder G2 variant configured for diverse global field layouts and wheel spacings. Uses 12x 240W diode lasers, 18 cameras, and 120 LED bedtop lights. Covers 0.75–1.50 ac/hr (0.30–0.61 ha/hr) with up to 5,000 weeds shot per minute and sub-millimeter accuracy. Designed for specialty crops on farms with non-standard track widths or row spacing.

name: LaserWeeder G2 200
desc: Smallest, lightest unit in the LaserWeeder G2 modular product line. At 6.6 ft (2.0 m) wide and 4,250 lbs (1,928 kg), it's designed for small specialty crop farms and easy transport between fields. Uses 8x 240W diode lasers (upgraded from 150W in Gen 1) for faster shoot times, plus dual NVIDIA GPUs and high-resolution cameras for sub-millimeter weed targeting accuracy. Twice the throughput of the original LaserWeeder per module.
camera_detail: Enhanced optics, high-resolution for sub-millimeter detection

name: Dyson Spot+Scrub™ AI Robot Vacuum Cleaner
desc: The Dyson Spot+Scrub AI (announced 2025) is Dyson's first vacuum-and-mop, adding a rotating mop pad that lifts away from carpet and AI dirt detection on top of Dyson's 360° vision navigation.
cameras: HD camera with green-spectrum LED illumination
mop_type: Rotating mop pad with auto-lift + dirt detection

name: ArmMotus EMU
desc: Fourier's ArmMotus EMU is a 3D back-drivable upper-limb rehabilitation robot built on a cable-driven mechanism with lightweight carbon-fibre rods to minimise friction and inertia. It delivers gravity-compensated, multi-directional movement training with haptic feedback and gamified exercises (table tennis, cooking, fishing), and supports bilateral mirror training. Award-winning (Red Dot 2022, iF 2022, IERA 2023).

name: ExoMotus X2
desc: Fourier's ExoMotus X2 is a lower-limb powered exoskeleton in the ExoMotus series, using a modular biped structure with flexible joint motors, motion controllers and multi-dimensional force sensors to deliver gait training for patients with lower-limb impairment, and serving as a research platform for developers.

name: MetaMotus Galileo
desc: Fourier's MetaMotus Galileo is an integrated VR-enhanced rehabilitation platform combining a treadmill, force plates and exoskeleton/upper-limb device integration (e.g. ExoMotus M4, dual ArmMotus EMU) for immersive gait, balance and motor training. Award-winning (Good Design Award, Shanghai Design 100+).
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for motion tracking and biomechanics analysis

name: CycleMotus A4
desc: Fourier's CycleMotus A4 is an active-and-passive cycling trainer for upper and lower limbs with motor-assisted resistance and a touchscreen interface, used for early mobilisation and endurance training in stroke, spinal-cord-injury and Parkinson's patients.

name: AnkleMotus
desc: Fourier's AnkleMotus (M1-A) is an ankle-joint rehabilitation robot providing active and passive movement training, strength and proprioception exercises for patients recovering ankle function after stroke or injury.

name: BalanceMotus KINE-SIM
desc: Fourier's BalanceMotus / Kine-Sim is a balance assessment and training system using a motion platform and interactive tasks to evaluate and retrain postural control, supporting fall-prevention and vestibular rehabilitation.
cameras: Integrated motion tracking cameras for posture analysis

name: HandyRehab
desc: Fourier's HandyRehab is a wearable hand-rehabilitation exoskeleton (robotic glove) that assists finger flexion/extension and grasp retraining, supporting task-oriented hand therapy for neurological patients.

name: ExoMotus M4
desc: Fourier's ExoMotus M4 is a powered lower-limb gait-training exoskeleton paired with a wheeled self-balancing frame, using in-house servo-motors and multi-dimensional force sensors for early-stage sit-to-stand and ambulation retraining.

name: ArmMotus M2 Pro
desc: Fourier's ArmMotus M2 Pro is an upper-limb rehabilitation robot for neurological and musculoskeletal disorders, using force-feedback technology to deliver adaptive, assist-as-needed movement support with planar reaching exercises and performance tracking.
cameras: Built-in monitoring camera for patient safety

name: Dexterous Hand
desc: Fourier's Dexterous Hand is a multi-finger robotic hand with tactile sensing developed as an end-effector for the company's GR-series humanoids, enabling fine grasping and manipulation.

name: GR-3
desc: Fourier GR-3 — care-oriented variant with soft tactile skin, designed for rehabilitation and elderly-care interaction. Repositioned by Fourier toward healthcare from pure industrial.
ai_model: Dual-path interaction: fast reflexes + LLM-driven contextual responses

name: GR-2
desc: Fourier's second-gen general-purpose humanoid. 53 DOF, FSA series actuators, 12-DOF dexterous hand. Targeted at research, education, rehabilitation, healthcare adjacent industrial work.
actuator_type: FSA 2.0 — 7 distinct actuator types, dual-encoder (2x control accuracy), serial joint architecture
sdk: Full SDK: ROS, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Mujoco + machine vision, path planning & force-feedback modules
hand_type: Dexterous 5-finger hands, 12 DoF each, 6 array-type tactile sensors (force, shape & material detection)
ai_model: Sim-to-real training: NVIDIA Isaac Gym → Isaac Lab

name: MiPA
desc: NEURA Robotics' MiPA ('My intelligent Personal Assistant') is a cognitive mobile-manipulator service robot with two fine-motor arms, autonomous navigation and a rich sensor suite. Powered by NEURA's AURA cloud AI and the Neuraverse app ecosystem (skills added like phone apps), it performs tasks such as vacuuming, unloading a dishwasher, tidying, beverage service and health monitoring for home, care and retail settings.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth sensors

name: MAV
desc: Multi-Sensing Autonomous Vehicle for indoor intralogistics, built to move larger, heavier goods than conventional AMRs — up to 1.5 tonnes on four lifting units for pallets. Navigates with 360° laser scanners at ±5 mm accuracy, supports hand-gesture control via 3D vision, shows status on side LEDs, and pairs with NEURA's LARA cobot or MAiRA for mobile manipulation.
use_cases: Pairs with LARA/MAiRA for mobile manipulation

name: LARA 10
desc: NEURA Robotics' LARA 10 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (10 kg payload) in the LARA (Lightweight Agile Robotic Assistant) line, offering cost-effective cobot automation within NEURA's cognitive-robotics ecosystem.
cameras: Integrated vision system with RGB cameras

name: LARA 5
desc: NEURA Robotics' LARA 5 is a 6-axis collaborative robot (5 kg payload) in the LARA (Lightweight Agile Robotic Assistant) line, offering cost-effective cobot automation within NEURA's cognitive-robotics ecosystem.
cameras: Integrated RGB-D camera for vision-guided applications

name: MAiRA M
desc: NEURA Robotics' MAiRA M is a mid-size MAiRA cognitive cobot - a sensitive, AI-enabled collaborative arm with integrated perception (vision, touch, voice) for cognitive automation and close human-robot collaboration.
cameras: Integrated 3D camera for AI-based object recognition

name: 4NE1 Mini
desc: NEURA Robotics' 4NE1 Mini is a smaller household-focused member of the 4NE1 humanoid family, aimed at domestic tasks such as cleaning, organizing, health monitoring and daily-routine support - bringing NEURA's cognitive robotics toward the consumer home.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth sensors for 360-degree perception

name: NEURA Quadruped
desc: NEURA Robotics' quadruped (Explorer) is a four-legged robot built for challenging terrain, carrying up to ~22 kg with 360-degree vision and running NEURA's Neuraverse OS for autonomous navigation. Targeted at mining, search-and-rescue and rugged industrial inspection, it was recognised with a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

name: Diana 7 (by Agile Robots)
desc: The Diana 7, from Agile Robots, is a 7-axis collaborative robot arm with torque sensors in every joint, a 7 kg payload, ~923 mm reach and ~0.05 mm repeatability. Its full force/torque sensing enables compliant, contact-rich manipulation, making it a popular platform for research and precision assembly.
cameras: Optional external cameras for vision applications

name: Franka Hand 3
desc: The Franka Hand 3 is a parallel-jaw gripper / end-effector for Franka Robotics arms (e.g. FR3), providing programmable-force grasping for sensitive assembly and research tasks.

name: Tactile Mobile Robot (TMR)
desc: Mobile robot base built for teleoperation, mobile manipulation and physical-AI research, natively compatible with the Franka Research 3 (FR3) arm. Pre-configured mechanical, electrical and software interfaces integrate it with FR3 Duo setups, and standardized mounting points let researchers add sensors and actuators. Supports 1 kHz control via the Franka Control Interface and is fully integrated with ROS 2.
highlights: 1 kHz control via Franka Control Interface

name: Mobile FR3 Duo
desc: The Mobile FR3 Duo pairs two 7-axis torque-sensing Franka FR3 arms on a mobile base for bimanual mobile manipulation, a research platform for compliant two-handed tasks.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth sensors integrated into mobile platform

name: CECIL (Consolidated Edison Combined Inspection and Lancing)
desc: CECIL (Consolidated Edison Combined Inspection and Lancing) is a specialized industrial robot for inspecting and lancing (cleaning) boiler tubes and confined industrial spaces, keeping workers out of hazardous maintenance environments.
cameras: Multiple inspection cameras for steam generator tube monitoring

name: Robotic Applique Kit (RAK-3)
desc: QinetiQ's Robotic Applique Kit (RAK) is a bolt-on system that converts manned military ground vehicles into optionally-manned/unmanned platforms. RAK-3 adds drive-by-wire actuation, teleoperation and waypoint autonomy so existing vehicles can be operated remotely for dull, dirty and dangerous missions such as route clearance, resupply and ISR.
cameras: Multiple day/night cameras for situational awareness

name: RCV-L (Robotic Command Vehicle - Light)
desc: QinetiQ's RCV-L (Robotic Combat Vehicle-Light), developed with Pratt Miller, is a ~3.9-tonne diesel-electric hybrid, rubber-tracked unmanned combat vehicle for the US Army's RCV programme. With a modular payload architecture carrying ~3,175 kg at over 60 km/h, it can be remotely controlled or driven semi-autonomously and is air-transportable to remote locations.
cameras: 360-degree situational awareness cameras, thermal imaging, electro-optical sensors

name: MAARS (Modular Advanced Armed Robotic System)
desc: QinetiQ's MAARS (Modular Advanced Armed Robotic System) is a tracked unmanned ground robot designed for reconnaissance, surveillance and target acquisition, able to mount a remote weapon station (such as an M240B machine gun or 40 mm grenade launcher). It lets forces apply firepower and ISR from forward positions while crews stay protected.

name: TALON V
desc: QinetiQ's TALON V is the modernised sixth-generation of the world-renowned TALON family, with 4,000+ units delivered. An IOP-first, modular tracked EOD/CBRN robot with heavy-lift manipulator, 16 I/O ports, HD and thermal cameras and JAUS interoperability, it performs bomb disposal, CBRN/HazMat reconnaissance, surveillance and comms-relay missions.
cameras: Day/night camera with zoom and thermal imaging capability

name: RT-7 (ROCU)
desc: The RoboTeam RT-7 is a ground robot operated via RoboTeam's ROCU controller, applied to inspection and industrial/security tasks. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against RoboTeam.)

name: RT-20 (MTGR)
desc: RoboTeam's MTGR (Micro Tactical Ground Robot, RT-20) is a rugged ~9 kg backpackable tracked robot with high manoeuvrability indoors and out. Widely used by the IDF in urban and tunnel environments, its intuitive ROCU control and modular payloads make it a go-to for military, law-enforcement and SWAT reconnaissance.
cameras: 360° PTZ camera with day/night vision, thermal imaging

name: RT-200 (TIGR)
desc: RoboTeam's TIGR (Transportable Interoperable Ground Robot, RT-200) is a medium two-man-carried UGV with best-in-class day/night vision and a 5-DOF manipulator with 2 m reach for EOD render-safe operations, IED search and CBRN survey. Its modular design accepts advanced manipulators and EOD/CBRN payloads.
cameras: 360-degree panoramic camera system with day/night vision capabilities

name: RT-1000 (PROBOT)
desc: RoboTeam's PROBOT (RT-1000) is a lightweight heavy-payload UGV that carries up to about three times its own weight (~750 kg) across sand, water and rubble on wheels or optional tracks. Operated via the ROCU controller, it supports logistics carry, casualty evacuation, CBRN and ISR missions while keeping soldiers at standoff.
cameras: Multiple HD cameras for navigation and surveillance

name: RT-2000 (ROOK)
desc: RoboTeam's ROOK (RT-2000) is a modular tracked UGV that hosts mission payloads for logistics, ISR and EOD/route-clearance tasks. Part of RoboTeam's interoperable family controlled from the ROCU, it brings heavier payload capacity than the backpackable MTGR while keeping rapid deployability.
cameras: Day/night vision cameras with thermal imaging

name: Intelligent Power Inspection Robot
desc: An intelligent power-inspection robot (a Teledyne FLIR partner product) that autonomously patrols electrical substations and power facilities, using thermal and visual imaging to detect hot spots and faults. (Partner product; detailed specs worth verifying.)
cameras: Thermal imaging camera, visible light camera

name: Guardian DX
desc: Sarcos' Guardian DX (now Palladyne) is a highly dexterous, force-reflective dual-arm robot that can be teleoperated with intuitive motion mirroring or run semi-autonomously, for dexterous work in hazardous or remote industrial environments.
cameras: Multiple HD cameras for operator vision and task monitoring

name: C200 RoboShuttle
desc: Bin-carrying RoboShuttle robot for high-density tote-to-person storage in narrow-aisle layouts. Lifts totes from mezzanine racking up to ~2.9 m and delivers them to picking stations. Certified 'Best of Intralogistics 2020' by the IFOY award.
cameras: Navigation cameras and QR code readers

name: P500R (P-Series)
desc: P-Series goods-to-person robot that lifts and moves racks and shelves to operators in automated warehouses. Compact body with a fast lifting response and inertial + QR-code navigation; adapts to varied floor and temperature conditions and is reported to cut manual labor by 50–70%.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and positioning

name: Porter
desc: Heavy-duty pallet-moving autonomous mobile robot that extends the 6 River / Ocado Mobile Robot System beyond picking, handling cross-docking, bulk-item picking, putaway and palletized inventory moves. Works the floor alongside Chuck under Ocado IQ system-directed orchestration.
highlights: Pairs with Chuck on the floor
cameras: 3D vision system with Fork Insertion Depth System (FIDS)

name: Chuck+
desc: Chuck, from 6 River Systems (Ocado Group), is a collaborative warehouse fulfillment robot that guides associates through pick paths and carries totes - boosting picking productivity without fixed infrastructure. 'Chuck+' denotes a newer generation.

name: Max
desc: The heavyweight LocusBot, designed for safe autonomous transport of large and heavy payloads — pallets, pallet-sized containers, cartons, totes and boxes. An industrial-strength chassis and omnidirectional mobility move up to 3,000 lb smoothly across industrial and material-handling facilities, coordinated as part of a multi-bot LocusOne fleet.
cameras: Multiple stereo cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: RightPick (Previous Generations)
desc: RightHand Robotics' RightPick is an AI-driven robotic piece-picking system (arm + adaptive gripper + vision) that grasps a wide variety of items for e-commerce and pharmacy order fulfillment. This record covers previous RightPick generations.
cameras: RGB-D camera for computer vision and object recognition

name: Coco Delivery Robot v3
desc: The third-generation Coco delivery robot continues Coco Robotics' remotely-piloted urban delivery approach with incremental autonomy and sensing upgrades for dense city food delivery.

name: Coco 1
desc: Coco 1 is Coco Robotics' purpose-built last-mile delivery robot. Unlike fully autonomous competitors, Coco's pink cargo bots are remotely piloted by human operators, focusing on reliable short-range food delivery in dense urban areas such as Los Angeles.

name: Kiwibot Warehouse Robot
desc: The Kiwibot Warehouse Robot is an autonomous mobile robot adapting Kiwibot's navigation stack for indoor warehouse material transport.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and object detection

name: ROSA Knee with OptimiZe
desc: The Zimmer Biomet ROSA platform assists in knee and hip replacement (and, in ROSA Brain/Spine versions, neurosurgery), providing data-driven planning and intraoperative guidance for implant positioning.
cameras: Multiple intraoperative cameras for real-time surgical field visualization and bone tracking

name: OTTAVA Robotic Surgical System

name: B2

Used for power-grid inspection, petrochemical patrols and factory operations.

name: Go2 Air

name: Go2 Pro

Dual cutting discs, 400mm cutting width.

name: GOAT A3000 LiDAR PRO
desc: Top-tier GOAT with 32V high-performance battery, dual blade-disc design, 400W max cutting power (3x efficiency vs standard). 3000m² coverage. Best Ecovacs for large complex yards. 400m²/h coverage rate.

name: GOAT O1000 LiDAR PRO
desc: Ecovacs entry-flagship 2026 wire-free mower for 1/4-acre lawns. HoloScope 360 Dual-LiDAR (mechanical 360° + 3D ToF solid-state) + AI camera, AIVI 3D obstacle avoidance (200+ types, 5cm precision). Built-in TruEdge trimmer for zero-edge cuts. 80cm narrow-path capability. IPX6.
use_cases: Compact residential lawns up to 0.3 acre

name: Landroid S WR165
desc: Compact Landroid for 1/8-acre lawns. Uses Worx 20V 2.0Ah Power Share battery (compatible with 35+ Worx tools). Floating blade disc auto-adjusts for uneven terrain. Patented AIA (Artificial Intelligence Algorithm) for narrow-passage navigation. Cut-to-Edge offset blades minimize trimming. Boundary wire required.
use_cases: Small residential lawns up to 1/8 acre

desc: Mid-size Landroid for 1/4-acre lawns. Worx 20V 4.0Ah Power Share battery. Four wheels for traction. Same AIA navigation and floating blade as S series, with longer runtime.

name: Landroid L WR155
desc: Large Landroid for 1/2-acre lawns. Worx 20V 6.0Ah Power Share battery, 115-minute charge time. Cloud computing for auto-scheduling based on local weather, season, grass species and sun radiation. OTA updates.

name: Landroid Vision WR235
desc: Worx camera-vision Landroid — wire-free, no antenna or boundary wire. AI camera trained on grass recognition. Works under tree canopy where satellite navigation fails. Major shift from wire-bound traditional Landroids.

name: Landroid Vision Cloud M1000
desc: Worx 2026 Vision Landroid with cloud-based AI for adaptive mowing. Camera navigation, OTA model updates from the cloud, no boundary wire.

name: Figure 03
desc: Figure AI's third-generation humanoid (unveiled October 2025). Built for the home alongside industrial deployment. Helix 2.0 vision-language-action model. Soft fabric exterior, mesh hair design. BMW Spartanburg production deployment for the Figure 02 fleet. Brett Adcock targets one million Figure 03 units across 4 years. Closed $1.5B Series C at $39.5B valuation Sept 2025.

name: Optimus Gen 3
desc: Tesla's third-generation Optimus, demonstrated 2026. Significant upgrade over Gen 2 — improved hands with biological-inspired tendon actuation, faster walking gait. Target: $25-30K consumer price at scale, with internal Tesla factory deployment first. Powered by Tesla Dojo training infrastructure.

name: Atlas (Hydraulic)
desc: The original hydraulic Atlas (2013) was built by Boston Dynamics for the DARPA Robotics Challenge - a 1.88 m, ~150 kg hydraulically actuated humanoid for disaster-response research. Successive versions grew dramatically more agile (parkour, backflips) before the hydraulic Atlas was retired in 2024 in favour of the all-electric Atlas.

name: Atlas (Electric)
desc: Boston Dynamics' fifth-generation Atlas — fully electric replacement for the hydraulic original. Unveiled April 2024 after the hydraulic Atlas's retirement. Production debut at CES 2026 with $420K initial pricing. Custom 3D-printed titanium/aluminum actuators (Hyundai Mobis). 360° hip/waist/neck rotation impossible for humans. Designed for industrial deployment at Hyundai Metaplant. 56 DOF, 50 kg payload, 2.3m reach. Powered by DeepMind Gemini Robotics models via Orbit platform.

name: NEO
desc: 1X Technologies' consumer-ready home humanoid. Pre-orders opened October 2025 at $20,000 (or $499/month subscription). First US deliveries scheduled 2026. Soft 3D-lattice polymer exterior + lightweight composite frame + tendon-drive joints make it human-safe. 22-DoF hands per side (44 total) for human-level dexterity. 22 dB acoustic profile — quieter than a refrigerator. OpenAI-backed. Powered by Redwood AI (video-trained World Model). NVIDIA Jetson Thor compute.
use_cases: Household humanoid — preorders open, first home deliveries 2026
Industrial expansion: up to 10,000 units to 300+ EQT portfolio companies (2026-2030)

name: A1
desc: AGIBOT's RAISE A1 (Aug 2023) was the company's first humanoid - a 175 cm, 53 kg, 49-DOF industrial biped that walks at ~7 km/h and handles loads up to 80 kg. Equipped with RGB-D and LiDAR sensors and modular components, it targets automotive, 3C-manufacturing, logistics and laboratory tasks like bolt-tightening and vehicle inspection.
use_cases: First-gen AGIBOT humanoid (debut Aug 2023): vehicle inspection, bolt tightening demos

name: A2
desc: AGIBOT (Zhiyuan Robotics, Shanghai) flagship full-size humanoid. AGIBOT shipped ~5,168 humanoids in 2025 — the world's #1 humanoid producer by volume per Omdia analyst firm. Held Guinness World Record for 106km autonomous walk Suzhou-to-Shanghai. 40+ DOF, 200 TOPS AI compute, GO-1 vision-language foundation model. Multi-region certified (China, US, Europe). PLd safety architecture with 360° perception.
ai_model: WorkGPT multimodal engine (~96% accuracy across text, audio & visual)

name: A3
desc: AGIBOT's A3 (Yuanzheng/Expedition A3, 2025) is a newer full-size humanoid in AGIBOT's rapidly expanding lineup. (Recent release - detailed specifications still being confirmed.)
use_cases: Next-gen Expedition humanoid (Aug 2025): industrial work, martial-arts agility demos, 10-hour endurance

name: Walker S1
desc: UBTECH's Walker S1 (2024) is an industrial humanoid designed for factory work - it has been trialled on automotive and electronics production lines (with partners including BYD and Foxconn) performing sorting, handling and inspection tasks as part of UBTECH's push into commercial humanoid labour.

name: Alpha 1E
desc: UBTECH's Alpha 1E (2018) is a 39 cm desktop educational humanoid with 16 servo joints, programmable for walking, dancing and choreographed routines via app or visual coding - an affordable platform for teaching robotics and programming.

name: IRON
desc: XPENG's IRON (Next-Gen, 2025) is a lifelike bipedal humanoid with a human-like flexible spine, full-body touch-sensing soft skin, up to 82 degrees of freedom (22 per hand) and three proprietary Turing AI chips (~2,250 TOPS) running XPENG's Physical World model. Built with solid-state batteries, XPENG targets mass production for retail, guidance and inspection roles.

name: K2
desc: Kepler's Forerunner K2 (Shanghai Kepler, 2024) is a full-size industrial humanoid - 178 cm, 85 kg, 52 DOF with 100 TOPS of compute and a 2.33 kWh battery good for an ~8-hour shift. Its tactile hands (96 fingertip sensors) handle ~15 kg per hand / 30 kg dual-arm, and a cloud cognitive model plus imitation/reinforcement learning drive autonomous task completion. Marketed as the company's fifth-generation design, also branded 'Bumblebee'/'Hornet'.

name: 4NE-1
desc: NEURA Robotics’ flagship cognitive humanoid and Europe’s first humanoid designed for series production. Standing 180 cm and 80 kg, the Gen 3.5 lifts up to 100 kg — the highest among general-purpose humanoids — via ~490 N·m leg joints. Co-designed with Studio F.A. Porsche, powered by NVIDIA Thor T5000 and Isaac GR00T, with full-body artificial skin for safe human collaboration. Premiered at Automatica 2025; Gen 3.5 from €98,000.

name: MiPa Gen 3
desc: NEURA Robotics' MiPA Gen 3 (2026) is the latest generation of the cognitive household/service mobile-manipulator, demonstrated at CES 2026 unloading dishwashers and monitoring vital signs. Powered by AURA AI and the Neuraverse app ecosystem, with global reservations open.

name: Sophia
desc: Hanson Robotics' Sophia (2016) is a highly expressive android famous for its lifelike face (Frubber skin) capable of dozens of expressions, conversational AI and global media appearances - even being granted symbolic Saudi citizenship. A platform for human-robot interaction research and AI demonstration.

name: TIAGo
desc: PAL Robotics' TIAGo (2018) is a mobile manipulator on a differential-drive base with a liftable torso and a 7-DOF arm - a modular, ROS-based research platform for service robotics, mobile manipulation and assistive applications rather than a bipedal humanoid.

name: TALOS
desc: PAL Robotics' TALOS (2017) is a 175 cm, 95 kg fully electric, torque-controlled humanoid built for research and industrial manipulation. With 32 DOF and EtherCAT torque-sensing joints, it can lift 6 kg per arm and serves as a high-end ROS research platform.

name: CyberOne
desc: Xiaomi's CyberOne (2022) is a 177 cm, 52 kg full-size bipedal humanoid with 21 DOF, emotion recognition and Xiaomi's self-developed actuators. Unveiled as a technology demonstrator showcasing Xiaomi's move into humanoid robotics.

name: STAR1
desc: RobotEra's STAR1 (2024) is a 171 cm, 55-DOF bipedal humanoid that set a world record for bipedal running at 3.6 m/s outdoors, with joints up to 400 N.m torque and direct-drive 12-DOF hands. Paired with RobotEra's ERA-42 AI model, it executes high-precision commercial tasks.

name: L7
desc: RobotEra's L7 (2025) is a next-generation full-size humanoid from the Chinese maker of the record-setting STAR1, advancing locomotion and whole-body manipulation. (Recent release - detailed specifications still being confirmed.)

name: S1
desc: Astribot's S1 (Stardust Intelligence, 2024) is a wheeled-base bimanual humanoid with 36 DOF (7 per arm) and exceptional manipulation speed, trained via imitation learning to cook, clean, pour drinks and play instruments. Launched at the World Robot Conference, it targets home, lab and hospitality tasks.

name: EM02
desc: EngineAI's EM-02 (Shenzhen, 2024) is an agile humanoid robot notable for dynamic motions including a demonstrated front flip, part of the wave of Chinese humanoid developers pushing athletic locomotion. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against EngineAI.)

name: DR01
desc: DEEP Robotics' DR01 (2024) is an agile quadruped from the Hangzhou-based maker of the Lite3 and X-series inspection robots, built for dynamic, high-speed legged locomotion and research. (Some detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against DEEP Robotics.)

name: N1
desc: Noetix Robotics' N1 (2024) is a humanoid from the Chinese maker known for aggressively low-priced humanoids, aimed at research, education and developers entering the field. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against Noetix.)

name: Promobot V4
desc: Promobot V.4 (2018) is a wheeled service humanoid with an expressive animatronic face, speech interaction and autonomous indoor navigation, deployed for reception, customer service, promotion and public information in malls, banks and airports.

name: Sprout
desc: Sprout is a humanoid robot from US startup Fauna Robotics (2025), an early-stage entrant in the general-purpose humanoid space. (Recent/limited public data - specifications worth verifying.)

name: T-HR3
desc: Toyota's T-HR3 (2017) is a 32-DOF teleoperated humanoid controlled via a wearable Master Maneuvering System and force-feedback, letting an operator remotely mirror movements and feel what the robot touches. A research platform for safe human-robot collaboration and remote work.

name: ASIMO
desc: Honda's ASIMO (2000-2018) was the world's most famous bipedal humanoid for two decades - 130 cm tall, it could walk, run at ~9 km/h, climb stairs, hop and recognise faces and gestures. A landmark in dynamic bipedal locomotion, it was retired in 2018 with its technology feeding Honda's later robotics work.

name: Pepper
desc: Pepper (SoftBank/Aldebaran, 2014) is a 120 cm social humanoid on a wheeled omnidirectional base with a chest tablet, designed to read emotions and interact in retail, reception and hospitality. Hugely visible in stores and research, production was paused in 2021.

name: NAO
desc: NAO (Aldebaran, later SoftBank Robotics) is a 58 cm, 25-DOF programmable humanoid that became the world's most widely used educational and research robot. With cameras, microphones and the NAOqi platform, it teaches coding and serves HRI research, autism therapy and classrooms globally.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 5
desc: Starship's six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery robot - the most-deployed in the world with 10M+ deliveries. It travels at pedestrian pace (~6 km/h) within ~2-3 km of a store, carrying up to 10 kg (about three shopping bags) in an app-locked insulated compartment. A bogie/six-wheel system climbs curbs; perception uses 12 cameras plus ultrasonic, radar and GPS. Operates at L4 with remote human assist and runs ~18 hours on a charge.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 6
desc: The sixth-generation Starship delivery robot refines the six-wheeled sidewalk platform with upgraded compute, sensing and world-first onsite wireless charging (overnight, no plug). It carries up to 10 kg in an insulated, app-locked compartment at pedestrian speed, operating ~18 hours per charge with winter wheels for snow. Part of the fleet that makes ~125,000 road/driveway crossings daily worldwide at L4 autonomy.

name: R1
desc: Nuro's R1 was the company's first-generation passengerless autonomous delivery vehicle, launched in Scottsdale, Arizona in December 2018 with Kroger - the first-ever unmanned delivery service for the general public. A compact, electric, road-going pod with no driver or passengers, built purely to carry goods.

name: R2
desc: The Nuro R2 was the first vehicle granted a USDOT/NHTSA self-driving exemption (no mirrors, pedals or steering wheel), debuting in Houston in 2020. A narrow, passengerless electric delivery pod (1150 kg, ~190 kg payload), it carries food, groceries and parcels at up to 40 km/h with a 360-degree suite of 12 cameras, top lidar plus 14 side lidars, dual IMUs and ultrasonics, with heating/cooling cargo bays.

name: R3
desc: Nuro's third-generation vehicle (2022) is its production-ready, passengerless delivery pod. About 20% narrower than an average car, it runs up to 72 km/h with double the R2's cargo - dual ~27 cu ft compartments holding ~227 kg / 24 grocery bags with modular heating and cooling. A pedestrian-protecting external front airbag is a world-first safety feature. Built for mass production with BYD.

name: Serve Gen 1
desc: Serve Robotics' first-generation low-emission sidewalk delivery robot, spun out of Postmates/Uber. A four-wheeled L4 bot with fail-safe mechanical braking and autonomous collision avoidance, it delivers food on sidewalks with remote human assist, deployed initially with Uber Eats in Los Angeles.

name: Serve Gen 2
desc: Serve Robotics' second-generation sidewalk delivery robot - the workhorse of its commercial Los Angeles fleet with Uber Eats. L4 autonomy with fail-safe mechanical braking, a multi-camera-plus-lidar sensor suite, and an app-locked cargo compartment for food and convenience orders.

name: Serve Gen 3
desc: Serve Robotics' third-generation sidewalk delivery robot, built for national scaling with 2,000 units rolling out from 2025. It moves roughly twice as fast and twice as far as Gen 2, adds ~6 hours of daily field time, and runs 5x more AI on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin module with Ouster's REV7 digital lidar. Emergency braking stops 40% more quickly, at roughly half the prior manufacturing cost.

name: Kiwibot 5.0
desc: Kiwibot 5.0 (2024) is the latest generation of Kiwibot's four-wheeled sidewalk delivery robot, with improved autonomy, sensing and cargo capacity over the 4.0, continuing the company's campus and urban last-mile food-delivery deployments.

name: Model C
desc: Cartken's six-wheeled Model C is a camera-SLAM autonomous delivery robot (a Google Area 120 spin-off) that operates both outdoors on sidewalks and indoors with elevator/multi-floor capability. It runs L4 autonomy with instant remote-operator override, carries ~20 kg / 30 L, and is assembled by Magna in Michigan. Deployed for food and campus delivery with Uber Eats and Grubhub, and increasingly for in-facility logistics.

name: Courier
desc: Cartken's Courier is the outdoor last-mile configuration of its six-wheeled, camera-SLAM delivery platform. Built for sidewalk food and grocery runs within a ~3-mile radius, it uses vision-only autonomy with remote-operator backup and is manufactured with Magna.

name: Coco 2
desc: Coco 2 (2024) is the next generation of Coco Robotics' urban delivery bot, adding more driver-assist autonomy on top of its remote-piloted model while keeping the insulated cargo compartment for food delivery across cities including Los Angeles and Miami.

name: REV-1
desc: Refraction AI's REV-1 is a three-wheeled delivery robot designed for bike lanes rather than sidewalks or full roads, giving it a speed-and-flexibility advantage. Running up to ~24 km/h with a camera-and-radar suite (no lidar) and remote supervision, it was piloted for grocery and meal delivery in Ann Arbor and Austin.

name: Tinymile
desc: Tinymile is a Toronto-based sidewalk delivery robot operated by remote human pilots, delivering food on city sidewalks. Its small, insulated cargo bot focuses on dense downtown restaurant delivery.

name: Tortoise
desc: Tortoise builds low-speed, remotely-managed delivery and repositioning robots for retail and residential communities. Its devices, tested by Walmart, are human-piloted remotely rather than fully autonomous, handling neighbourhood grocery delivery and shared-cart repositioning.

name: Avride Robotaxi
desc: Avride's robotaxi runs the company's Level 4 autonomy stack (spun out of the former Yandex self-driving group) on production EV platforms, partnered with Uber. Avride also operates a large Uber Eats delivery-rover fleet across Dallas, Austin and Jersey City, with robotaxi expansion planned into Munich.
manufacturer_history: Autonomy team spun out of Yandex self-driving group

name: Clevon 1
desc: Clevon 1 (from Estonia's Clevon, formerly Cleveron Mobility) is a compact, road-legal autonomous delivery carrier. Electric and passengerless, it carries modular cargo at up to ~50 km/h under L4 autonomy with teleoperation oversight, targeting grocery and retail last-mile.

name: Meituan RB1
