desc: Second of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. Identical hardware to Honey and Bumble (the blue one of the trio), used for autonomous navigation research, payload transport, and remote inspection inside the station. Queen was the first Astrobee to fly fully in 2019.

name: Astrobee Bumble
desc: Third of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. The blue/yellow striped one of the trio. Used for autonomous flight research, environmental monitoring, and supporting astronaut activities through teleoperation or scripted behaviors. Replaced an earlier-generation robot called SPHERES.

name: CIMON
desc: Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Spherical AI assistant developed by Airbus and IBM (Watson) for DLR. Operated briefly on the ISS in 2018, designed to assist astronauts with experiments and provide voice-controlled information retrieval. Used 14 internal impellers for free-flight in microgravity. Pioneered AI-driven crew companionship in space.

name: CIMON-2
desc: Second-generation Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Improved AI emotional sensitivity (using Watson Tone Analyzer), longer battery life, and more robust flight capability than CIMON. Operated on the ISS from 2019 with multiple successful astronaut interaction sessions including with ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano.

name: Double 3
desc: The third-generation Double Robotics mobile telepresence robot. Introduced dual cameras with 13-megapixel stills and 150° wide-angle obstacle avoidance, plus a beamforming microphone array. Superseded by Double 4 in late 2024.

name: Double 4
desc: Fourth-generation flagship mobile telepresence robot from Double Robotics, unveiled November 2024. Improved obstacle avoidance, sturdier base for uneven floors, and seamless integration with Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet.
secondary_camera: Floor camera with HDR night vision

name: Double 2
desc: The robot that defined the consumer telepresence category. Self-balancing two-wheel base with iPad as the screen and brain, allowing remote workers to attend meetings, walk hallways, and tour facilities from anywhere.

name: BeamPro
desc: Enterprise telepresence robot that defined the high-end remote-presence category. Used widely in tech-company offices including by Edward Snowden remotely. Original Suitable Technologies wound down in 2020; brand revived with Beam Pro 3 in 2025.

name: Beam Pro 3
desc: Third-generation Beam Pro announced May 2025 as Suitable Technologies' return to the market. Features higher-resolution 4K video, improved battery life, and enhanced enterprise management tools.

name: Ohmni Supercam
desc: OhmniLabs' next-generation flagship launched March 2025, featuring ultra-high-resolution 4K camera and AI-powered auto-framing for healthcare, enterprise collaboration, and distance learning.

name: Ohmni
desc: OhmniLabs' original consumer-friendly mobile telepresence robot. Lightweight three-wheel design with HD video and tilt-screen mechanism for natural eye contact. Widely deployed in healthcare and remote-work contexts.

name: Temi
desc: Autonomous mobile robot blending telepresence with personal-assistant functionality. Uses 3D vision and LiDAR for autonomous navigation, can follow users, dock automatically, and deliver items between rooms.
languages_spoken: English, Mandarin, Hebrew, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Arabic

name: Temi Pro
desc: Business-focused Temi launched July 2024 with enhanced autonomy, 4K camera, and improved navigation. Targeted at retail, healthcare, hospitality, and corporate deployments where reliability and fleet management matter.

name: Ava Telepresence
desc: Enterprise-grade autonomous telepresence robot built on Ava Robotics' navigation platform (spun out from iRobot). Self-navigates to meeting rooms, integrates with Cisco Webex and Microsoft Teams, and added AI environmental sensors via Cisco partnership in 2025.

name: VGo
desc: One of the earliest commercial telepresence robots. Widely deployed in K-12 schools to let homebound students attend classes, and in hospitals for remote patient consultations. Acquired by Vecna Technologies in 2015.

name: Anybots QB
desc: One of the first commercial telepresence robots. Self-balancing two-wheel design predated Double Robotics. Anybots discontinued the QB by 2014 before relaunching as Anybots 2.0 with industrial focus.

name: Anybots QX
desc: Industrial-focused telepresence robot completing beta testing in September 2024 with commercial launch Q2 2025. Ruggedized for remote industrial inspections in manufacturing and oil & gas, with thermal imaging and multi-terrain mobility.

name: Giraff
desc: Eldercare-focused telepresence robot for the European market. Used in numerous EU-funded research projects on independent living for older adults. Brand later transitioned to Camanio Care.

name: Teladoc InTouch Lite
desc: Clinical-grade telepresence robot for hospital deployments. Originally from InTouch Health (acquired by Teladoc in 2020 for $600M), used in stroke care, ICU consultations, and tele-ICU programs across major hospital networks worldwide.

name: Kubi
desc: Tabletop telepresence robot — a pan/tilt cradle for an iPad. Let remote participants look around a meeting room rather than being stuck with a fixed laptop view. Acquired by Xandex in 2017.

name: MantaroBot
desc: US-made mobile telepresence platform with customizable hardware configurations. Used by enterprise and government customers including military training and remote inspection applications.

name: PadBot U1
desc: Budget consumer mobile telepresence robot from Chinese manufacturer Inbot Technology. Mounted a tablet on a self-balancing base, targeting small-business and personal use cases at a fraction of premium-brand pricing.

name: Texai
desc: Research telepresence prototype from Willow Garage (also the birthplace of ROS and PR2). Internal deployment at Willow Garage allowed remote employees to be present in the office. Never sold commercially but influenced the entire category.

name: PARO
desc: The original therapeutic social robot. Modeled on a baby harp seal, PARO is the longest-deployed eldercare robot worldwide with documented clinical benefits for dementia patients — reducing agitation and improving mood. FDA-cleared as a Class 2 medical device since 2009.

name: ElliQ 3
desc: Tabletop AI companion designed as a proactive engagement partner for older adults living alone. Deployed by New York State Office for the Aging and other US agency programs. Initiates conversations, sets medication reminders, leads cognitive exercises, and connects family via video call.
pilot_customers: NY State Office for the Aging

name: Moxie
desc: Companion robot for children ages 5-10 developed by Embodied (founded by former iRobot CTO Paolo Pirjanian). Used conversational AI and expressive animations to help kids develop emotional and social skills. Embodied wound down operations in late 2024 but units remain in active use.

name: Miko 3
desc: AI-powered conversational companion for children ages 5-10 combining play and STEM education. Indian unicorn valued at $550M with strong global sales. Includes built-in tablet face, voice interaction, and content library covering math, science, reading.

name: Miko Mini
desc: Compact, lower-cost sibling to Miko 3. Same conversational AI but in a static tabletop form. Targets gift-buyer parents at the sub-$150 price point and has been a strong holiday seller in US/UK markets.

name: Lovot
desc: Non-verbal emotional companion robot designed by ex-Pepper engineer Kaname Hayashi. Recognizes family members, responds to touch and voice, exhibits learned attachment behaviors. Wildly popular in Japan — sold tens of thousands of units despite the high price point.
shell_material: Soft fabric outer body, ABS frame

name: Jibo
desc: The world's first commercial social robot for the home. Developed by MIT Media Lab's Cynthia Breazeal. Sold from 2017-2018, NTT Disruption acquired remnants in 2020. Cult following — its 'final goodbye' update in 2019 became a viral cultural moment about emotional bonds with robots.

name: Pepper
desc: Iconic humanoid social robot deployed in retail, hospitality and research worldwide. Sold over 20,000 units. SoftBank Robotics halted production in 2021. Aldebaran filed for bankruptcy in 2025, leaving thousands of deployed units without official support.
languages_spoken: 15+ including English, French, Japanese, Mandarin, Spanish

name: NAO
desc: Iconic small humanoid robot used in education, autism therapy, and research worldwide. Over 13,000 units deployed across 70+ countries. Aldebaran's bankruptcy in 2025 halted production though many units remain in active research and educational use.
languages_spoken: 20+ languages including English, French, German, Japanese, Mandarin, Spanish, Arabic

name: Vector 2.0
desc: Revived version of the original Anki Vector after Digital Dream Labs acquired the IP in 2020. Compact desktop companion with personality, voice interaction, Alexa integration, and local processing for privacy.

name: Cozmo
desc: Tabletop personality robot from Anki with expressive facial animations and code-with-Cozmo programming feature. Anki shut down in 2019. Massively influential in the AI-personality category — many of today's social bots draw lineage from Cozmo's design language.

name: Loona
desc: Expressive smart pet robot from Shenzhen-based KEYi Tech. Combines lifelike animations, voice recognition, and emotion-detection AI. Successfully Kickstarted in 2022 raising over $4M, has shipped to 60+ countries.

name: Eilik
desc: Affordable desktop personality robot that went viral via TikTok. Two units can interact and chat with each other. No app, no subscription, no internet required — runs offline with built-in personality scripts.

name: Qoobo
desc: Therapeutic robotic cushion with a moving tail. No face, no voice — just a tail that responds to touch like a cat. Designed for people who can't keep pets (apartments, allergies, eldercare). Won multiple design awards including Red Dot.

name: Hyodol
desc: ChatGPT-powered companion doll deployed at scale in South Korea. Over 12,000 units distributed by Korean municipal governments to elderly living alone. Tracks medication, provides conversation, alerts emergency contacts when issues arise.

name: Abi
desc: AI-powered eldercare companion robot from Melbourne-based Andromeda Robotics. Raised $17M in March 2026 to expand into the US senior care market. Deployed across Australian aged-care homes with focus on cognitive engagement and dignified assistance.

name: Ryan
desc: Tabletop social robot from DreamFace Technologies (University of Denver spin-off) featuring an animated face projected onto a translucent 3D head. Used in dementia care research and clinical settings — focused on engaging conversations with cognitively impaired adults.

name: Buddy
desc: Family-oriented social robot from French startup Blue Frog Robotics. Funded via Indiegogo, shipped 2018. Designed to be a household assistant, security monitor, and child companion. Company restructured in 2024 ending consumer sales.

name: Kuri
desc: Family home companion from Mayfield Robotics (a Bosch subsidiary). Cute design with autonomous navigation, no face screen — communicated entirely through eye animations and chirps. Bosch shut down Mayfield in 2018 before mass shipping. All customer deposits were refunded.

name: BDX Droid
desc: Disney's autonomous interactive Star Wars droid character — short for 'Bipedal Dynamic Experiment.' Variants include OSKAR-7 (orange), BESH-27 (blue), GREK-17 (green), Red. Won the 2025 Thea Award for Technical Innovation. Roams Galaxy's Edge at Disneyland, Disney World, Tokyo Disneyland, Disneyland Paris and Shanghai Disneyland. Debuts on screen in The Mandalorian and Grogu (May 2026). Patent filed October 2023 as 'walking robots.'
ai_model: Disney Research autonomous behavior model (RL + Imitation)

name: Project Kiwi (Baby Groot)
desc: Free-walking autonomous Baby Groot character developed by Disney Imagineering as a milestone in expressive character robotics. Pint-sized humanoid with accurately rendered face/hands/feet, distressed red flight suit, expressive eye contact. The Project Kiwi platform later evolved into the BDX droid program. Stages controlled meet-and-greet appearances.

name: Walt Disney – A Magical Life
desc: Audio-Animatronic figure of Walt Disney himself, opened July 17 2025 at Disneyland California for the park's 70th anniversary. Plays in rotation with Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln (1964). 17-minute stage show in the Main Street, USA section. Controversial — Walt's granddaughter Joanna Miller publicly opposed the robot likeness, calling it 'dehumanizing.'
pilot_customers: Disneyland Park, Main Street USA (Disneyland Opera House)

name: ADAM
desc: Dual-armed AI-powered bartender (Automated Dual Arm Mixologist) from NASDAQ-listed Richtech Robotics. Debuted at CES 2024. First robot bartender permanently stationed at a major league sports venue (Texas Rangers Globe Life Field, 2024). Now serving at T-Mobile Arena NHL games. 23-drink menu, NSF certified for food service.
form_factor: Dual-arm robotic torso on counter base
pilot_customers: T-Mobile Arena Las Vegas (NHL Golden Knights)

name: Makr Shakr (Toni)
desc: Two-armed robotic bartender installation co-designed with MIT and Pentagram design studio. Permanently installed on Royal Caribbean's Quantum-class cruise ships, airports, hotels and event spaces worldwide. Compatto model adds coffee; Veloce model can make up to 250 drinks per hour. Pioneered the robotic bartender category.

name: Kuratas
desc: Pilot-operated 4-meter mecha from Japanese artist Kogoro Kurata. Famous for the 2017 international mecha duel against MegaBots Inc.'s Eagle Prime (USA). Available for purchase or rental for events. Combines theatrical scale with a working piloted cockpit. Controlled via Kinect-style motion or smartphone.
actuator_type: Diesel-powered, four-wheeled rolling base, hydraulic arms; V-Sido control system (cockpit or smartphone piloting)
use_cases: The original commercial pilotable mecha (from ~US.35 million)
Fought MegaBots in the 2017 USA-vs-Japan giant robot duel

name: Stickboy (Compressorhead drummer)
desc: Four-armed pneumatic drummer in the world's first robotic heavy metal band Compressorhead. Built by German engineers from steel auto parts. Has played live across Europe and Australia, opened for Black Sabbath at Wacken Open Air 2016. The full band includes Bones (bass), Fingers (guitar), and Hellga (vocals).

name: Z-Machines
desc: Japanese all-robot band consisting of MACH (78-finger guitarist), ASHURA (22-arm drummer), and COSMO (laser keyboardist). Created by Naofumi Yonetsuka (Tokyo University), performed at SXSW 2013 and Tokyo. Squarepusher composed 'Music for Robots' EP specifically for them in 2014. Project paused after 2015.

name: Blue (Newton-trained BDX)
desc: Fully autonomous BDX-style droid unveiled by Jensen Huang at NVIDIA GTC 2025. Collaboration between NVIDIA, Google DeepMind, and Disney Research. Trained in NVIDIA's Newton physics engine (jointly developed by all three companies) using Isaac GROOT N1 Humanoid Foundation Model. No remote control — fully AI-driven walked on stage with Huang.
ai_model: NVIDIA Isaac GROOT N1 Humanoid Foundation Model

name: Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln
desc: The original full-body Audio-Animatronic figure, debuted at the 1964 New York World's Fair (Illinois Pavilion) and moved to Disneyland in 1965. Has been periodically updated — most recent overhaul 2009 includes more lifelike skin texturing and facial expressions. Foundational milestone of the entire animatronic category, predating Disney's other animatronic shows by decades.
mobility: Static (stands from chair, gestures, hand movements)

name: Bobo and Olive (Sky Force Snack Bar)
desc: Pair of robotic characters serving snacks at the Cosmic Rewind area in Walt Disney World EPCOT. Interact with guests via scripted humorous banter while assisting human cast members. Example of Disney's expansion of robotics from passive animatronics to active service roles.
pilot_customers: Walt Disney World - EPCOT - Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind

name: Shadow Dexterous Hand
desc: Anthropomorphic robotic hand widely used in research, prosthetics development, and entertainment installations. Most human-like robotic hand on the market. Has appeared in art installations including 'In Event of Moon Disaster' at the Imperial War Museum. Used by OpenAI for dexterous manipulation research.

name: Rovio
desc: WiFi-controlled mobile webcam robot from WowWee, designed for home telepresence and remote monitoring. Found a niche in event entertainment as a remotely-operated 'roving reporter' character at conferences and live shows. Discontinued in consumer market.

name: RoboSapien
desc: Mass-market biomorphic robot designed by NASA roboticist Mark Tilden. Sold over 7 million units worldwide making it one of the best-selling robot toys in history. Used in countless trade shows, music videos and entertainment events. Defined the home humanoid toy category and predates almost every modern consumer social robot.

name: Spot
desc: The category-defining commercial quadruped. Released 2019 by Boston Dynamics (then Google/Alphabet, now Hyundai-owned). Used worldwide for industrial inspection, construction site documentation, public safety, research, and entertainment. Over 1,500 units deployed across 30+ countries. Lease price $74,500.

name: Spot Enterprise
desc: Enterprise variant of Spot with self-charging dock, expanded autonomy, and Scout management software. Targets continuous unmanned inspection deployments. Adds 4G LTE option and enhanced safety features over base Spot.

name: Spot with Arm (SpotArm)
desc: Spot equipped with the Boston Dynamics manipulator arm. Adds 7-DOF arm with gripper enabling door-opening, valve-turning, picking up objects, and remote manipulation in hazardous environments. ~$200K total with arm + Spot.

name: Go1
desc: Unitree first-generation Go-series quadruped. Predecessor to Go2. Featured "intelligent side-follow" mode tracking owner via stereo cameras. Mass-market price ($2,700) made it the first sub-$3K quadruped with real autonomy. Largely superseded by Go2 line.

name: ANYmal D
desc: Industrial inspection quadruped from ETH Zurich spin-off ANYbotics. Used by BP, Shell, Petronas, and major chemical plants for autonomous routine inspection. IP67 rating, ATEX-compliant Ex-Proof variant available. Now in its D-version (ANYmal D, 2023).

name: CyberDog 2
desc: Xiaomi second-generation consumer quadruped, refined from CyberDog (2021). Bio-mimetic Doberman-inspired design. Open-source platform with NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, AI vision (face/gesture/voice recognition), and developer SDK. Targets developers and tech-enthusiast consumers.
cameras: AI camera + Intel RealSense D430 depth + ultra-wide fish-eye

name: X50 Ultra
desc: The Dreame X50 Ultra (2025) delivers 20,000 Pa suction and a ProLeap chassis that physically steps over thresholds and obstacles up to ~6 cm. DuoScrub rotating mops, detangling main brush, 360 navigation and a 75 C hot-water self-cleaning dock.
mop_type: DuoScrub dual rotating mop pads (extendable MopExtend)

name: X40 Ultra
desc: The Dreame X40 Ultra (2024) combines 12,000 Pa suction with fully removable, liftable DuoScrub rotating mops, an extending side brush and mop for edges, and 70 C (158 F) hot-water mop & washboard self-cleaning, plus auto-empty and auto-refill. LiDAR + AI navigation.
mop_type: DuoScrub dual rotating mop pads (extendable MopExtend)

name: X40 Master
desc: The Dreame X40 Master is a variant of the X40 Ultra platform with 12,000 Pa suction, liftable DuoScrub rotating mops, extending side brush, 70 C hot-water mop self-cleaning and full auto-empty/refill dock.
mop_type: DuoScrub dual rotating mop pads (extendable MopExtend)

name: L40 Ultra Gen 2
desc: The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 (2025) hits 25,000 Pa suction and adds a TriCut hair-cutting main brush that slices tangled hair into the dustbin, plus DuoScrub extendable rotating mops, 58 C hot-water mop washing and a 100-day auto-empty dock.
mop_type: DuoScrub dual rotating mop pads (extendable MopExtend)

name: L50 Ultra
desc: The Dreame L50 Ultra (2025) pairs 19,500 Pa suction with the ProLeap System that climbs thresholds up to ~6 cm and a VersaLift navigation module that retracts the LiDAR to clean under low furniture. DuoScrub rotating mops, full hot self-cleaning dock.
mop_type: DuoScrub dual rotating mop pads (extendable MopExtend)

name: D10s Plus
desc: The Dreame D10s Plus offers 5,000 Pa suction with a flat drag mop, LiDAR navigation and a self-emptying dock for hands-off dust disposal.

name: Deebot X8 Pro Omni
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot X8 Pro Omni (2024) introduces an OZMO Roller mop - a spinning roller continuously fed with fresh water and scraped clean in real time, scrubbing rather than smearing - paired with 18,000 Pa suction, TruEdge adaptive edge mopping, AIVI obstacle avoidance and a 75 C hot-water self-cleaning, detergent-dosing dock.
mop_type: OZMO Roller - spinning roller mop with continuous fresh-water wash

name: Deebot X2 Omni
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot X2 Omni (2023) adopts a square-front chassis for better edge and corner reach, with 8,000 Pa suction, dual rotating OZMO mops, AIVI 3D 3.0 obstacle avoidance and a full OMNI dock with hot-water mop washing, drying and auto-refill.

name: Deebot T50 Pro Omni
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot T50 Pro Omni (2024) is a slim (81 mm) 15,000 Pa cleaner with dual rotating OZMO mops, low-profile dToF navigation to slide under furniture, AIVI obstacle avoidance and a full hot-water self-cleaning OMNI dock.

name: X10 Pro Omni
desc: Eufy's X10 Pro Omni (2024) delivers 8,000 Pa suction with dual rotating mop pads that auto-lift 12 mm over carpet, AI obstacle avoidance, and an Omni dock that auto-empties, washes/dries the mops and refills water.
mop_type: Dual rotating mop pads (12 mm auto-lift)

name: Omni E25
desc: The Eufy Omni E25 pairs 8,000 Pa suction with dual rotating mops and a full Omni self-cleaning dock, LiDAR navigation.

name: Roomba Max 10

name: Bespoke AI Jet Bot Steam Ultra
desc: The Samsung Bespoke Jet Bot Combo (2023) is Samsung's flagship vacuum-and-mop with AI object recognition, LiDAR navigation and an all-in-one Clean Station that empties dust and washes/steams the mop pad.

name: A2 Max
desc: AGIBOT's A2 Max is the heavy-duty industrial member of the A2 family - larger and heavier at 175 cm and ~85 kg - presented for material handling and palletizing, a step beyond the service orientation of A2 Lite/Ultra.

desc: The Roborock Qrevo Edge (2024) raises suction to 18,500 Pa HyperForce with a DuoDivide anti-tangle brush and adds FlexiArm extending mops and side brush for true edge-to-edge coverage. Dual spinning pads, 75 C hot-water mop wash and warm-air drying in the dock, PreciSense LiDAR plus Reactive AI obstacle recognition.
mop_type: Dual spinning mop pads + FlexiArm extending edge mop

name: L9000
desc: The L9000 is a robot vacuum and mop from Tikom that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: Q6 Pro
desc: The Q6 Pro is a robot vacuum and mop from Honiture that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: S8 MaxV Ultra
desc: Roborock's S8 MaxV Ultra is the 2024 apex of the S8 line: 10,000 Pa HyperForce suction, a DuoRoller dual rubber brush, and a VibraRise 2.0 sonic mop scrubbing at 4,000 times/min that lifts 20 mm over carpet. Reactive AI 2.0 pairs 3D structured light with an RGB camera to recognise 73 object types, and the 8-in-1 RockDock Ultra auto-empties (~7 weeks), washes the mop in up to 60 C hot water, dries it, and refills the robot's 100 ml tank from a 4 L clean-water supply. 5,200 mAh battery, ~180 min runtime, ~300 m2 per charge.
mop_type: VibraRise 2.0 dual sonic vibrating mop (4,000/min) + rotating edge mop
navigation: PreciSense LiDAR + Reactive AI 2.0 (3D structured light + RGB camera, 73 objects)

name: Chang'e 3 Lander
desc: China's Chang'e 3 lander (2013) achieved the first soft lunar landing since 1976, touching down in Mare Imbrium and deploying the Yutu rover. It carried cameras, an extreme-ultraviolet telescope and ground-penetrating instruments, operating for years beyond its design life.

name: Chang'e 4 Lander
desc: China's Chang'e 4 lander (2019) made the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon, in Von Karman crater, relaying data via the Queqiao relay satellite and deploying the Yutu-2 rover for the longest-running lunar surface mission.
payload_instruments: Biological Experiment Payload (carried cotton seeds — first plant grown on Moon)

name: Chang'e 5 Lander
desc: First lunar sample return mission since the Soviet Luna 24 in 1976. Landed in Mons Rümker region of Oceanus Procellarum on 1 December 2020, used a robotic arm and drill to collect 1.731 kg of lunar regolith, and launched it back to Earth via the ascent stage on 3 December. Samples were the youngest ever collected from the Moon (~2 billion years old), reshaping understanding of lunar volcanism.
mission_status: Decommissioned (ascent stage returned samples to Earth)

name: VIPER
desc: Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover. Golf-cart-sized rover designed to search for water ice at the lunar south pole. Originally targeting a 2023 launch on Astrobotic's Griffin lander, then cancelled by NASA in July 2024 to cut costs, but revived in September 2025 with Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 as the new delivery vehicle. Will be the first rover specifically designed to operate in permanently shadowed lunar regions.
actuator_type: 4 independently steered wheels with active suspension
launch_vehicle: Blue Origin New Glenn (via Blue Moon Mark 1 lander)
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery (designed for cold lunar night survival)

name: Peregrine Mission One
desc: Astrobotic's Peregrine (Jan 2024) was a commercial CLPS lunar lander; a propellant leak after launch prevented a Moon landing and it was guided to re-enter Earth's atmosphere - a notable milestone attempt in commercial lunar robotics.
payload_instruments: 20 commercial and government payloads including 5 NASA CLPS instruments: Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer (LETS)
outcome: Propellant leak after launch; controlled Earth re-entry (no landing)

name: Nova-C IM-1 (Odysseus)
desc: First US spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972, and first commercial soft landing in history. Landed near the lunar south pole at Malapert A crater on 22 February 2024 but tipped over on landing after a leg broke, limiting science operations. Most payloads remained functional. Used methalox propulsion — first to use it in deep space.
also_known_as: Odysseus, Odie, IM-1, CLPS Task Order 2-IM
target_body: Moon (Malapert A crater, south pole region)
payload_instruments: Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS)
Plus 6 commercial: ILO-X telescope, EagleCam camera, etc.

name: Nova-C IM-2 (Athena)
desc: Intuitive Machines' second lunar lander mission, launched 27 February 2025. Touched down at Mons Mouton near the lunar south pole on 6 March 2025 but landed on its side inside a crater approximately 250 m from the intended site. Mission ended within a day due to inability to recharge solar panels. Carried the Micro-Nova Hopper, the MAPP rover, and PRIME-1 ice-drilling experiment.
also_known_as: Athena, IM-2, CLPS Task Order CP-11
mission_type: Commercial lunar lander (CLPS) with rover and hopper
payload_instruments: PRIME-1 (Polar Resources Ice Mining Experiment): TRIDENT drill + MSolo mass spectrometer

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
desc: First fully successful commercial lunar landing in history. Landed upright in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille on 2 March 2025, completing all primary mission objectives over 14 Earth days. Operated 10 NASA CLPS science payloads on the lunar surface. First mission to capture a GPS lock from the Moon and high-resolution video of a lunar sunset. Powered down for lunar night on 16 March 2025.
also_known_as: BGM1, Ghost Riders in the Sky, CLPS TO 19D
payload_instruments: 10 NASA CLPS payloads: Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE)
Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS)
Lunar Instrumentation for Subsurface Thermal Exploration with Rapidity (LISTER)

name: Hakuto-R Mission 1
desc: First commercial lunar landing attempt by a private Japanese company. Launched 11 December 2022, successfully reached lunar orbit, but crashed during landing attempt on 25 April 2023 due to an altitude sensor misreading caused by passing over the rim of Atlas Crater. Carried the UAE's Rashid rover and JAXA's transformable SORA-Q technology demonstrator (which was reflown on SLIM in 2024).
payload_instruments: Rashid rover (UAE Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre — first Arab Moon mission)
AI flight computer (Mission Control Space Services)

name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience)
desc: ispace's Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience, 2025) was a Japanese commercial lunar lander carrying the Tenacious micro-rover. Like Mission 1 (2023), it reached lunar orbit but did not achieve a successful soft landing, as ispace continues developing commercial cislunar transport.

name: Griffin Mission One
desc: Astrobotic's Griffin Mission 1 is a large commercial lunar lander developed under NASA's CLPS programme. Originally tasked with delivering NASA's VIPER rover (later removed by NASA), Griffin is one of the biggest US commercial landers, designed to carry substantial payloads to the lunar surface.
payload_instruments: VIPER mass simulator (replacing cancelled VIPER rover)

name: Int-Ball
desc: JEM Internal Ball Camera. Small spherical free-flying camera drone deployed inside Japan's Kibo module on the ISS in 2017. Designed to reduce the workload of astronauts who previously spent ~10% of their time on photo/video documentation. Diameter just 15 cm — could be deployed and recovered by hand. Operational until 2019.
also_known_as: JEM Internal Ball Camera, JEM Int-Ball

name: Int-Ball2
desc: Second-generation Int-Ball, launched to the ISS in February 2024. Improved autonomous navigation using stereo vision (replacing ultrasonic sensors), higher-resolution 4K camera, AI-based image processing, and longer battery life. Continues the mission of automated visual documentation inside the Kibo module while reducing astronaut workload.

name: MEV-1
desc: Mission Extension Vehicle 1. First commercial satellite servicing spacecraft in history. Successfully docked with Intelsat IS-901 on 25 February 2020 in geostationary graveyard orbit, providing 5 years of station-keeping and attitude control to extend the host satellite's operational life. Demonstrated that on-orbit life extension is commercially viable.
actuator_type: Liquid apogee engine + hall-effect electric thrusters
payload_instruments: Rendezvous Proximity Operations and Docking (RPOD) sensors
Docking probe (engages Liquid Apogee Engine nozzle)
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery + hydrazine + Xenon

name: MEV-2
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Extension Vehicle-2 (MEV-2) docked with the Intelsat 10-02 communications satellite in 2021 to take over station-keeping and attitude control, extending the client's operational life - the second operational commercial life-extension servicer after MEV-1.
actuator_type: Liquid apogee engine + hall-effect electric thrusters
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery + hydrazine + Xenon

name: Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV)
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) is a next-generation servicing spacecraft equipped with robotic arms (developed with DARPA) to inspect client satellites and install Mission Extension Pods, enabling a scalable in-orbit life-extension service rather than one dedicated servicer per client.
actuator_type: Robotic arm with brushless DC motors + Hall-effect electric thrusters
mission_type: Robotic satellite servicer with manipulator arm
power_source: Solar array + Li-ion battery + Xenon ion propulsion

name: Mission Extension Pods (MEPs)
desc: Northrop Grumman's Mission Extension Pods (MEPs) are small propulsion 'jetpacks' that the Mission Robotic Vehicle attaches to a client satellite to provide years of additional station-keeping - a lighter, lower-cost alternative to a full Mission Extension Vehicle per satellite.

name: OSAM-1 (Restore-L)
desc: NASA's OSAM-1 (On-orbit Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing-1, formerly Restore-L) was designed to robotically rendezvous with and refuel the Landsat 7 satellite and demonstrate in-space assembly/manufacturing using dexterous robotic arms. NASA cancelled the project in 2024 amid cost and technical challenges.
also_known_as: On-orbit Servicing Assembly and Manufacturing 1, Restore-L (legacy)

name: Robonaut 2 (R2)
desc: First humanoid robot in space. Developed jointly by NASA Johnson Space Center and General Motors. Launched to the ISS on STS-133 in February 2011 initially as a torso-only humanoid restricted to a stanchion. Mobility legs added in 2014 to allow movement inside the station. Returned to Earth in 2018 for repairs after a hardware malfunction; planned to return to ISS.
operating_agency: NASA Johnson Space Center / General Motors

name: Valkyrie (R5)
desc: Full-size bipedal humanoid built by NASA's Johnson Space Center in just 15 months for the 2013 DARPA Robotics Challenge. Designed for potential deployment in space exploration scenarios including pre-deployment site preparation on Mars. Several units placed at research institutions (MIT, IHMC, Northeastern) for continued development.

name: Skybot F-850 (FEDOR)
desc: Russian humanoid robot, originally developed as FEDOR (Final Experimental Demonstration Object Research) for rescue and emergency operations by the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations. Adapted for space testing as Skybot F-850. Launched to the ISS on the uncrewed Soyuz MS-14 in August 2019. Conducted brief manipulation experiments before returning to Earth in September 2019. Mixed results — struggled in microgravity.

name: Kirobo
desc: Second humanoid robot in space (after Robonaut 2) and the first robot to hold a conversation in space. Tiny 34 cm humanoid developed by Toyota, University of Tokyo, Dentsu, and JAXA. Launched to the ISS on the Kounotori 4 cargo vehicle in August 2013 to serve as a communication companion for Japanese astronaut Koichi Wakata. Conducted Japan's first 'robot conversation in space' on 7 August 2013.
operating_agency: JAXA / University of Tokyo / Toyota / Dentsu / Robo Garage

name: ELSA-d
desc: Astroscale's ELSA-d (End-of-Life Services by Astroscale-demonstration, 2021) was a two-spacecraft mission - a servicer and a client - that demonstrated repeated magnetic capture and release of a client satellite in orbit, proving core technologies for future debris removal.
payload_instruments: Client satellite with magnetic plate (105 kg)

name: ADRAS-J
desc: Astroscale's ADRAS-J (Active Debris Removal by Astroscale-Japan, 2024) rendezvoused with and closely inspected a derelict Japanese H-IIA rocket upper stage - the first commercial mission to safely approach and survey a large piece of real space debris, a key step toward future removal.
target_body: Low Earth orbit (H-IIA upper stage, 600 km)

name: ELSA-M
desc: Astroscale's ELSA-M is a commercial debris-removal servicer designed to capture and de-orbit multiple defunct satellites in a single mission, building on ELSA-d to provide an operational end-of-life service for satellite operators.
payload_instruments: Magnetic capture plate (compatible with OneWeb satellites)

name: ClearSpace-1
desc: ClearSpace-1 is an ESA-contracted active-debris-removal mission led by Swiss startup ClearSpace, designed to rendezvous with and capture a derelict payload adapter using a four-arm tentacle-like capture mechanism, then de-orbit it - one of the first dedicated debris-capture missions.
target_body: Low Earth orbit (VESPA payload adapter, 800 km)
payload_instruments: Four robotic arms with clamping jaws

name: B1 (Black Line)
desc: Lighter, faster Black Line grid robot with a cavity design roughly half the footprint of the R5. Uses individual direct-drive wheel motors and a swappable BattPack lithium-ion battery, giving about 75% higher acceleration and ~20% higher bin throughput than the R5, and can carry taller bins.
highlights: Cavity design ~half the size of R5

name: Origin
desc: The original, category-defining LocusBot — a nimble goods-to-person AMR built for collaborative, high-volume order fulfillment. Works alongside human pickers to roughly double productivity by eliminating walking time, and supports dynamic task-interleaving of picking and putaway. Configurable with multi-level shelving and a range of containers, using LiDAR and vision navigation. Sold via Robots-as-a-Service.

name: MiR250
desc: Compact, agile autonomous mobile robot from MiR (Teradyne) carrying up to 250 kg at 2 m/s. With a 580×800 mm footprint and ~30 cm height it slips through gaps as narrow as 80 cm and uses lifts and doors autonomously, navigating by laser scanners and 3D cameras under MiR Fleet. Modular tops (Hook, Top Roller, shelf lift) adapt it to many tasks.
api: MiR Fleet; REST API; WMS integration

name: MiR600
desc: IP52-rated pallet-transport AMR from MiR moving up to 600 kg at 2 m/s — the first IP52-rated AMR on the market, able to withstand dust and water drops for more demanding environments. Designed to ISO 3691-4 safety standards, with modular pallet-lifter and conveyor tops and MiR Fleet orchestration.

name: MiR1350
desc: MiR's most powerful AMR, moving loaded pallets and heavy goods up to 1,350 kg on a 1,304×864 mm load surface. IP52-rated with 13 TÜV-certified safety features and ISO 3691-4 compliance, it pairs pallet-lifter tops with MiR Fleet for autonomous heavy intralogistics.

name: OTTO 100
desc: Strong, agile light-duty AMR from OTTO Motors (Rockwell Automation) that moves boxes, bins and carts up to 150 kg at 2 m/s through person-to-person workflows. An integrated lift works with carts, laser and 3D-camera sensors enable autonomous navigation, and the rugged body is built to shrug off forklift collisions.

name: OTTO 600
desc: Tough, nimble mid-payload AMR from OTTO Motors moving up to 600 kg through high-traffic, tight spaces. The narrowest footprint in its class with an all-metal IP54 body; two forward cameras plus dual 360° corner LiDARs handle perception, and rapid-access drawers make single-person servicing simple.

name: OTTO 1500
desc: Heavy-duty workhorse AMR from OTTO Motors that moves up to 1,900 kg at top speeds of 2 m/s, even around turns, in demanding industrial environments. Built on a proven chassis introduced in 2015 with 4M+ hours of operational runtime, it supports a wide range of attachments and a modular top panel for quick servicing.
highlights: Up to 1,900 kg payload at 2 m/s

name: Proteus
desc: Amazon's first fully autonomous mobile robot, built to operate in the same open floor space as employees rather than caged areas. It autonomously lifts and moves wheeled GoCarts of packages through fulfillment and sort centers, projecting a green light ahead and stopping if a person steps into its path. Named after a moon of Neptune; used internally across Amazon's network (not sold commercially).
highlights: Works in open, shared human spaces

name: Hercules
desc: Amazon Robotics drive unit — the modern successor to the Kiva drives — that slides under inventory pods and lifts up to ~567 kg (1,250 lb) to bring goods to stationary pickers. A forward-facing 3D camera identifies people, pods and other robots for safe, fast decisions, and thousands coordinate per site as a fleet under centralized planning. First widely deployed mobile robot certified to Safety Integrity Level (SIL) 2.

name: Aqua10 Ultra Roller
mop_type: AquaRoll roller mop - continuous fresh-water 4-step cycle (spray, scrub, squeeze, refresh) with counter-spinning FluffRoll
navigation: AI obstacle avoidance + structured light + RGB camera; ProLeap suspension
desc: Dreame's Aqua10 Ultra Roller (Sep 2025 flagship) replaces spinning pads with an AquaRoll roller mop that runs a continuous fresh-water spray-scrub-squeeze-refresh cycle, so it mops with clean water instead of pushing dirty water around. 30,000 Pa Vormax suction (Dreame's highest), a counter-spinning FluffRoll to lift fibres, AutoSeal carpet guard, and a ThermoHub dock with 100 C hot-water roller wash + 70 C hot-air dry. Climbs ~42 mm single / ~60 mm tiered thresholds. AU RRP ~A$2,799.

name: Aqua10 Ultra Track S
mop_type: TrackMop roller - sprays ~45 C hot water, scrubs, and extracts dirty water continuously in real time (no smearing)
navigation: AI cameras + structured light; VersaLift + ProLeap threshold climbing
desc: Dreame's Aqua10 Ultra Track S (Nov 2025) uses a TrackMop roller that sprays ~45 C hot water, scrubs, then continuously extracts the dirty water in real time - reviewers note it leaves tile genuinely clean and fast-drying with no sticky footprints, unlike pad-style bot-mops. 30,000 Pa Vormax suction, Mop-Extend side reach, auto-lift over carpet, VersaLift + ProLeap climbing to ~6 cm, and a ThermoHub self-cleaning dock. AU RRP A$2,999.

name: Matrix10 Ultra
mop_type: Multi-Mop Switching System - dock swaps heated mop pads per room; pads stay hot while mopping
navigation: Advanced AI navigation + structured light; cross-country threshold climbing
desc: Dreame's Matrix10 Ultra is billed as the world's first robot vacuum with a Multi-Mop Switching dock - a three-solution compartment that swaps mop pads per room and keeps them heated while mopping, plus dual cleaning/pet-odour solution dosing and dirt detection that re-passes stains. 30,000 Pa suction and advanced threshold-climbing navigation. AU RRP A$3,499.

name: Flow 2
mop_type: Roller mop with warm-water flow and real-time self-cleaning
navigation: Dual 1080p RGB cameras + AI obstacle detection
desc: The Narwal Flow 2 (CES 2026) is Narwal's new flagship, raising rated suction to 30,000 Pa and continuing the warm-water roller-mop system introduced on the original Flow, with real-time roller self-cleaning. Navigation moves to dual 1080p RGB cameras with AI-based real-time object detection and path planning.

name: Freo Z10 Turbo
desc: The Narwal Freo Z10 Turbo (CES 2026) offers 25,000 Pa suction with CarpetFocus technology, upgraded obstacle avoidance and a fully self-cleaning dock, building on Narwal's Freo Z line.

name: Deebot X12 OmniCyclone
mop_type: OZMO Roller 3.0 - 26 cm self-washing roller mop with stain pretreatment
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone (CES 2026) is built around the new OZMO Roller 3.0 system - a 26 cm self-washing roller (~50% longer than the prior version) - with front-facing stain pretreatment jets and a bagless OmniCyclone dust-separation dock. A CES 2026 standout for mopping performance.

name: Deebot T90 Pro Omni
mop_type: OZMO Roller 3.0 - 26 cm self-washing roller mop
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Omni (CES 2026) brings the 26 cm OZMO Roller 3.0 self-washing mop and fast PowerBoost charging to a more accessible tier, with an automated Omni Station designed to cut maintenance.

name: Omni S2
mop_type: Roller mop with continuous fresh-water wash + onboard dirty-water tank
desc: The Eufy Omni S2 (2026) uses a continuously-washed roller mop - wetted with clean water then scraped into an onboard dirty-water tank - succeeding the Omni S1 line, with a full self-cleaning dock and LiDAR + AI navigation.

name: Mobius 60
mop_type: Dual spinning mop pads - three interchangeable pad textures for different floors
desc: The MOVA Mobius 60 (CES 2026) introduces three interchangeable mop-pad textures matched to different floor surfaces, with dual spinning pads that self-clean at the base station. MOVA is a Dreame sub-brand.

name: X60 Max Ultra Complete
mop_type: DuoScrub dual spinning mop pads (self-cleaning at dock)
desc: The Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete (2026) is a top-tier vacuum-and-mop with DuoScrub dual spinning pads that self-clean at the dock, succeeding the X50 Ultra in Dreame's flagship line.

name: PowerDetect UV Reveal
desc: The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal (2026) is positioned as SharkNinja's most premium robot vacuum-and-mop, adding UV-based dirt detection on top of the PowerDetect cleaning system and a self-cleaning base.

name: EksoNR
desc: The clinical standard for rehabilitation walking. EksoNR’s SmartAssist software adapts help to each patient, and it was the first exoskeleton FDA-cleared for stroke and acquired brain injury, later expanded to SCI and MS.

name: Ekso Indego Personal
desc: Notable for being modular and light: Indego breaks into five pieces that assemble around a seated user, weighs ~12 kg, and is FDA-cleared for both clinical rehabilitation and personal use. Originally developed at Vanderbilt University.

name: EksoEVO
desc: A passive industrial vest, not a powered medical device. Ekso EVO supports raised arms using spring tension — no motors or battery — transferring overhead-work load to the hips. Widely deployed in automotive and aerospace assembly.

name: ReWalk Personal 6.0
desc: The best-known personal exoskeleton, commercially available since 2012. The 6th-generation ReWalk Personal is custom-built to each user’s measurements, drops the shoulder backpack of earlier models, and reaches 0.71 m/s — the fastest of any exoskeleton of its era. FDA-cleared and adopted by the US Department of Veterans Affairs.
actuator_type: Electric hip + knee actuation, tilt-sensor gait triggering
control_method: Tilt-sensor gait initiation from center-of-gravity shifts (crutches required)

name: ReStore
desc: A lightweight soft exosuit rather than a rigid frame. ReStore uses textile components and a cable-driven actuator to assist ankle movement during post-stroke gait therapy, making it one of the lightest clinical rehabilitation exoskeletons. FDA-cleared in 2019.
actuator_type: Soft exo-suit, powered ankle plantarflexion assist

name: HAL (Hybrid Assistive Limb)
desc: The original wearable cyborg. Cyberdyne’s HAL reads faint bioelectric (EMG) signals on the skin before the muscle moves, then drives powered hip and knee joints to assist — the medical lower-limb suit weighs ~23 kg, runs ~2h40m per charge, and was the first robot certified to the ISO 13482 personal-care safety standard. FDA-cleared in the US in 2018.
actuator_type: Electric, triggered by bioelectric signals (BES) from skin sensors

name: Cray X
desc: The first fully connected industrial exoskeleton. The 5th-generation Cray X is a carbon-fiber power suit giving up to 30 kg of lift support plus active walking assistance, running a full 8-hour shift on hot-swappable 40 V batteries. IP54-rated, it streams ergonomic telemetry to German Bionic’s AI and is used at BMW, IKEA and DPD.
use_cases: Industrial lifting injury prevention (BMW, IKEA, DPD)
assist_force: Up to 30 kg (66 lb) per lift
control_method: Dual servo motors, AI-adaptive (Smart Safety Companion)

name: Apogee
desc: German Bionic’s 6th-generation suit, leaner and lighter than the Cray X, with dual-motor support for lifting (up to 30 kg) and walking. The Apogee Ultra shown at CES 2025 pushes assist to 80 lb (36 kg), targeting baggage handling, construction and nursing.
actuator_type: Active electric back support, walking assistance

name: Atalante X
desc: The first crutchless self-balancing walking exoskeleton. Atalante X balances itself across 12 powered joints, freeing the patient’s hands entirely during gait therapy. CE-marked, deployed in rehab clinics across Europe and the US.
actuator_type: 12 powered joints (hips, knees, ankles), self-balancing dynamic walking

name: Eve
desc: Wandercraft’s personal-use exoskeleton, bringing self-balancing hands-free walking into daily life. In clinical trials and being industrialized with Renault Group.
use_cases: Personal hands-free mobility (clinical trials; Renault manufacturing partnership)

name: X-ble Shoulder
desc: Hyundai's X-ble Shoulder is a passive industrial wearable that supports overhead work, reducing shoulder-muscle load; part of Hyundai Robotics' wearable robot line (alongside earlier VEX/CEX) aimed at factory ergonomics.
actuator_type: Passive carbon-composite torque module (2.9–3.7 kgf assist, no battery)

name: MATE-XT
desc: A passive, batteryless shoulder exoskeleton from Comau weighing ~3 kg. MATE-XT mirrors arm movements with spring support across 8 levels and resists dust, UV and water for outdoor use in agriculture, construction and shipbuilding.
actuator_type: Passive spring-based shoulder support (8 adjustment levels, no battery)

name: Paexo Shoulder
desc: One of the lightest industrial exoskeletons at just 1.9 kg. Ottobock’s Paexo Shoulder is passive, transferring the weight of raised arms from the shoulders to the hips during overhead assembly. Deployed at Volkswagen.
control_method: Mechanical weight transfer to hips (no battery)

name: MyoPro
desc: A powered arm brace controlled by the wearer’s own body. MyoPro reads EMG signals from a weakened arm and drives a powered elbow and hand to complete the intended motion.
control_method: EMG signals from the wearer’s own arm

name: Ascend
desc: A featherweight exoskeleton that runs on air. Roam’s Ascend uses lightweight pneumatic actuation instead of motors, sensing movement to assist the knee — aimed at osteoarthritis and general mobility.

name: Carbonhand
desc: A soft robotic glove that adds strength to a human grip. Carbonhand’s fingertip sensors detect grasping, then artificial tendons add up to ~20% more force — used medically for weak hands and industrially to prevent strain.
actuator_type: Soft robotic glove with artificial tendons & fingertip force sensors
control_method: Fingertip pressure sensors + artificial tendons (SEM technology)

name: REX
desc: A self-supporting exoskeleton that stands on its own — no crutches required. REX bears its full weight independently and is joystick-driven, letting users with significant paralysis stand, walk and exercise hands-free.
actuator_type: Self-supporting powered legs, joystick control (no crutches)

name: Stretch 3
desc: Hello Robot's Stretch 3 is a lightweight (~24.5 kg) mobile manipulator built for research and assistive robotics - a wheeled base with a telescoping lift arm and dexterous wrist/gripper, fully ROS 2 native. Designed for in-home and lab manipulation studies at a fraction of the cost of traditional research arms.

name: Husky UGV
desc: The Clearpath Husky is a rugged medium-sized unmanned ground vehicle widely used in robotics research (including Mars robotics work at NASA/MIT). Large payload and power capacity, all-terrain differential drive, fully ROS 2 supported - the go-to outdoor research UGV.

name: Jackal UGV
desc: The Clearpath Jackal is a compact, weatherproof unmanned ground vehicle with onboard computer, GPS and IMU, used for outdoor autonomy, mapping and demining research. Comprehensive ROS API; popular in academia.

name: Dingo
desc: The Clearpath Dingo is a lightweight indoor mobile robot for research and education, available in differential or omnidirectional drive, used for navigation, mobile manipulation and mapping studies.

name: Ridgeback
desc: The Clearpath Ridgeback is an indoor omnidirectional mobile base designed to carry manipulators and heavy payloads, using mecanum-style wheels for precise forward, lateral and twisting motion - a common base for mobile-manipulation research.

name: Warthog UGV
desc: The Clearpath Warthog is a large amphibious all-terrain UGV for rugged outdoor research - capable on land, mud, snow and water - with high payload and ROS support for field robotics.

name: TurtleBot 4
desc: TurtleBot 4 is the world's leading low-cost open-source ROS 2 mobile robot, built on iRobot's Create 3 base with a Raspberry Pi 4, 2D LiDAR and OAK-D camera. The de-facto entry platform for learning ROS 2; available in Lite and Standard.

name: TurtleBot 3
desc: TurtleBot 3 (ROBOTIS, 2017) is a small, affordable, highly modular ROS mobile robot for education and research, available in Burger and Waffle Pi variants, with 360° LiDAR and Dynamixel actuators - a SLAM/navigation learning staple.

name: Human Support Robot (HSR)
desc: Toyota's Human Support Robot (HSR) is a compact, cylindrical mobile manipulator with a folding arm and omnidirectional base, developed for assistive and human-support research. It anchors the RoboCup@Home Domestic Standard Platform League.
cameras: RGB-D head camera + stereo + wide-angle cameras

name: Fetch
desc: The Fetch mobile manipulator (Fetch Robotics, now Zebra) pairs a round mobile base with a 7-DOF arm and adjustable-height torso, widely used in manipulation and warehouse-automation research; typically paired with the Freight base-only platform.

name: PR2
desc: The Willow Garage PR2 (Personal Robot 2) was the seminal dual-arm mobile-manipulation research platform that catalysed the ROS ecosystem. Two 7-DOF arms, an omnidirectional base and rich sensing - hugely influential, now discontinued but historically pivotal.

name: iCub
desc: iCub is an open-source child-sized (~104 cm) humanoid research platform from the Italian Institute of Technology, with ~53 DOF, rich tactile skin and vision, used worldwide to study embodied cognition, manipulation and human-robot interaction.

name: ALOHA 2 (Stationary)
desc: Trossen's ALOHA platform (based on the Stanford ALOHA project) is a low-cost bimanual teleoperation-and-imitation-learning system using paired leader/follower WidowX arms - a key platform for robot-learning and dexterous-manipulation research.

name: Reachy 2
desc: Reachy 2 (Pollen Robotics, now part of Hugging Face) is an open-source humanoid research robot with two 7-DOF bio-inspired arms, an expressive head and a mobile base option, designed for manipulation, teleoperation and embodied-AI research.

name: Nova Carter
desc: Nova Carter is NVIDIA's reference autonomous mobile robot for research and development on Isaac, integrating the Nova Orin sensor/compute architecture (multi-camera, LiDAR) for mapping, navigation and embodied-AI experimentation.

name: Stuntronics
desc: Stuntronics is Disney Imagineering's autonomous acrobatic robot - a self-correcting aerial performer that can flip and strike heroic poses mid-air, used for stunt doubles of characters (e.g. Spider-Man over Avengers Campus). It senses its body angle and rotation in flight to land poses precisely.

name: Vyloo
desc: Vyloo are small autonomous creature robots from Disney Imagineering (debuted around the Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge / parks R&D) that operate without external control, expressing curiosity and personality; staff can adjust their behaviour parameters to create new characters guests interact with.

name: RoboCoaster
desc: The KUKA RoboCoaster is an industrial-robot-based amusement ride that straps guests into a giant articulated arm for programmable motion sequences - used in attractions worldwide (e.g. Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey-style ride systems and Robocoaster G2 dark rides).
actuator_type: Based on KUKA KR 500 6-axis industrial arm

name: Kime
desc: Kime by Macco Robotics is a robotic beverage-and-food kiosk that autonomously pours beers and serves drinks/snacks at high throughput, deployed in stadiums, transport hubs and events as automated hospitality entertainment.

name: Cecilia
desc: Cecilia.ai is an interactive robotic bartender - a screen-faced AI persona with a robotic cocktail-mixing arm that chats with guests, takes orders by voice and mixes drinks, used at events, casinos and venues as conversational hospitality entertainment.

name: EX Robots Humanoid Android
desc: EX Robots (EX Future Technology, Dalian) builds hyper-realistic humanoid androids with silicone faces and many facial actuators for lifelike expressions, displayed in the company's humanoid museum and used for exhibitions and interactive entertainment.

name: GoBe
desc: GoBe (Blue Ocean Robotics) is an enterprise telepresence robot with autonomous navigation, HD video and a tall display, marketed around cutting business travel and CO2 - each unit can offset several tons of travel emissions per user annually. Used in offices, factories and healthcare.
use_cases: Telepresence for offices, healthcare & education (autonomous navigation + mapping)

name: OhmniCare
desc: OhmniCare (OhmniLabs, now part of Symbotic) is a healthcare-focused telepresence robot that replaced the original Ohmni in 2024, with a fully emotive neck, 4K video and one-click connection, designed for remote clinical rounds, tele-nursing and patient consults.
use_cases: Healthcare telepresence — remote patient visits & senior care

name: A2
desc: The AMY Robotics A2 is an autonomous-navigation telepresence robot with an adjustable-height display, HD camera and obstacle avoidance, used for remote office presence, healthcare rounds and remote inspection.
use_cases: Healthcare & office telepresence with autonomous navigation

name: PadBot P3
desc: The PadBot P3 (Inbot Technology) is a mid-size telepresence robot with a built-in HD display and camera (no tablet required), remote-driveable via app for home, office and education remote-presence use.

name: Ballie
desc: Ballie is Samsung's bright-yellow rolling home AI companion, powered by Google Gemini and Samsung's own models. It holds natural conversations, controls smart-home devices, greets visitors, projects content via a built-in projector, and checks on pets/family with front 4K and rear 2K cameras. Launch slated for 2026.

name: Q9 (CLOi AI Agent)
desc: LG's Q9 is a two-legged-wheeled home AI agent (part of the CLOi line) that moves around the home, recognises faces and emotions, and uses generative AI (integrating large language models) to manage smart-home routines and provide companionship.
use_cases: AI home agent: voice assistant, smart-home hub, patrol (announced CES 2025)

name: Ropet
desc: Ropet is a fluffy AI companion pet (CES 2025) with expressive screen-eyes that recognises faces, gestures and emotions, reacts with joy/affection/hunger, and converses via large language models in 50+ languages. ~600 g, ~2 h runtime on a 30-min charge, wireless charging dock.
use_cases: Palm-sized emotional companion (responds to touch, voice & warmth)

name: Moflin
desc: Moflin (Casio) is a small fluffy mood-syncing companion robot that uses emotional AI to develop a unique personality and bond with its owner over time, responding to handling with sounds and movement. ~5 h battery; aimed at stress relief and comfort.

name: Mirumi
desc: Mirumi (Yukai Engineering, CES 2025) is a small sloth-like companion robot that clings to bags or surfaces and reacts shyly when looked at or approached, designed purely to be endearing and reduce stress.

name: EMO
desc: EMO (Living.ai) is a desktop AI companion pet with 1,000+ expressions and movements; it tracks voices, recognises up to 10 people and objects, navigates the desk without falling, plays music and games, and acts as a small smart-home helper.
cameras: HD wide-angle camera (face recognition, up to 10 people) + 4-mic array

name: Jennie
desc: Jennie (Tombot) is a hyper-realistic robotic puppy designed as a therapeutic companion for people with dementia, anxiety or in elder care - it responds to touch and voice with lifelike movements and sounds, providing comfort without the demands of a live pet.

name: Astro
desc: Amazon Astro is a wheeled home robot combining Alexa, autonomous navigation, a periscope camera and visual/voice recognition for home monitoring, security patrols and companionship. Sold by invitation; positioned as a mobile household assistant.

name: B2-W
desc: The Unitree B2-W is a wheeled-leg variant of the B2, adding powered wheels at the feet for fast, smooth rolling on flat terrain while retaining legged ability to climb and traverse obstacles - notable for agile hybrid locomotion demos.

name: X30
desc: The DEEP Robotics X30 is a heavy-duty industrial quadruped with up to 40 kg payload, IP67 protection, operation from -20°C to 55°C and 3-4 h battery, with optional autonomous patrol software. Used in power-plant, mining and construction inspection; positioned as a lower-cost Spot rival.

name: Lite3
desc: The DEEP Robotics Lite3 is an affordable, lightweight (~11 kg) quadruped for locomotion and AI research, carrying up to ~5 kg, popular with universities in Asia and Europe; offers good SDK support for robot-learning work.

name: X20
desc: The DEEP Robotics X20 is an industrial inspection quadruped predecessor to the X30, with all-terrain mobility, thermal/gas sensor payloads and autonomous patrol for substations, tunnels and plants.

name: AlphaDog
desc: The Weilan AlphaDog is a quadruped built for security patrols, with integrated surveillance cameras, alert systems and 5G connectivity for autonomous monitoring; also marketed in consumer/companion variants.

name: B1
desc: The Unitree B1 was Unitree's first industrial-grade quadruped with IP68 protection and ~20 kg payload, used for inspection in harsh environments. Superseded by the more capable B2.

name: FIFISH V-EVO
desc: The QYSEA FIFISH V-EVO is a prosumer underwater drone with full 360° omnidirectional movement, a 4K UHD 60 FPS camera, AI Vision Lock subject tracking, 5,000-lumen lights and FPV goggle control - rated to ~100 m for inspection, filming and research.

name: Explorer
desc: The Saildrone Explorer is a wind-and-solar-powered uncrewed surface vehicle with 12+ months of endurance, used for ocean-data collection, bathymetric mapping, fisheries and maritime-domain awareness with a minimal carbon footprint.

name: Surveyor
desc: The Saildrone Surveyor is a large (~20 m) uncrewed surface vessel for deep-ocean bathymetric and acoustic mapping - one mission mapped ~90,000 km² of deep water - offering ship-grade survey at a fraction of crewed-vessel cost.
use_cases: Autonomous ocean-floor mapping (multibeam sonar to 7,000 m)

name: X3
desc: The Blueye X3 is a professional underwater drone (ROV) with three guest ports for sensors/tooling (grippers, sonar, lasers), HD camera and ~305 m depth rating, used for inspection, aquaculture and research.
use_cases: Research & aquaculture (3 guest ports: sonar, grippers, sensors)

name: iBubble
desc: iBubble (Notilo Plus) is a wireless autonomous underwater camera drone that follows and films a diver hands-free using acoustic tracking, rated to ~60 m - aimed at recreational and professional dive filming.

name: M2 Pro
desc: The Chasing M2 Pro is a versatile underwater ROV with omnidirectional movement, 4K camera and accessory mounts (grabber arm, sonar), rated to ~150 m, used for filming, inspection and light recovery.
use_cases: Industrial underwater inspection to 150 m depth

name: BIKI
desc: BIKI (Robosea) is a compact bionic fish-shaped underwater drone that swims with a tail fin for quiet, low-disturbance filming, with a 4K camera and ~60 m depth rating - a consumer-oriented bionic aquatic robot.

name: Thermite RS3
desc: The Howe & Howe Thermite RS3 is a remote firefighting robot on industrial tank treads - 24 hp diesel, climbs ~70 deg slopes, and blasts up to ~2,500 gal/min of water or foam. Built for refinery, HAZMAT and industrial fires (BLEVEs).

name: Thermite RS1
desc: The Howe & Howe Thermite RS1 is a compact remote firefighting robot on tank treads with a diesel powerplant, designed to enter structures and industrial fires too dangerous for crews and deliver high-volume water/foam streams.

name: EMILY
desc: EMILY (Hydronalix) is a ~4-ft, ~12 kg remote-controlled rescue flotation robot reaching ~10 m/s (23 mph), used to reach drowning victims fast; it helped rescue 240+ refugees off the Greek coast and can act as a flotation platform for several people.

name: Velox
desc: Velox (Pliant Energy Systems) is an amphibious robot propelled by undulating silicone fins, able to swim, skate on ice and push through snow - suited to cold-water and ice rescues where humans cannot safely approach.
use_cases: Amphibious operations: swims, crawls, traverses ice & sand

name: Sigma
desc: Fotokite Sigma is a fully-autonomous tethered drone for first responders that launches from a vehicle and holds persistent aerial thermal/visual overwatch of an incident, giving commanders continuous situational awareness without a trained pilot.
feature: Persistent thermal/visual overwatch; no pilot needed
use_cases: Persistent aerial situational awareness for first responders (24 h flight, no pilot licence)

name: Snakebot
desc: The CMU Snakebot (Biorobotics Lab) is a many-jointed serpentine robot that crawls and climbs through rubble and pipes inaccessible to people or dogs - deployed after the 2017 Mexico City earthquake and used for infrastructure inspection.
use_cases: Search & rescue in rubble, pipes & confined spaces

name: MV-4
desc: The DOK-ING MV-4 is a compact remote-controlled demining machine using a flail/tiller to safely detonate and clear landmines, widely deployed for humanitarian mine clearance in former conflict zones.

name: TAF 35
desc: The Magirus TAF 35 is a remote-controlled tracked firefighting robot with a large turbine that atomises and projects water/foam at high volume over long distances - for tunnel fires, industrial blazes and scenarios too hazardous for crews.

name: Dino
desc: The Naïo Dino is a large-scale autonomous weeding robot for vegetable farms, straddling beds to mechanically remove weeds with interchangeable tools, RTK-GPS guided and fully electric.
use_cases: Autonomous mechanical weeding for vegetable row crops

name: MK-V
desc: The Monarch MK-V is a 70 hp fully-electric driver-optional smart tractor: up to ~14 h battery (5-6 h recharge), IP65, 4WD, swappable battery packs and onboard power outlets, with camera-based autonomy and per-acre data collection. Suited to vineyards, orchards, dairy and solar-farm vegetation management; cuts ~2 t CO2/year on a 50-acre farm.

name: Solix Ag Robot
desc: The Solinftec Solix is a lightweight, solar-powered, 100% autonomous field robot that scouts crops (corn, soy, wheat, cotton), detects pests and disease, and applies targeted spot-spraying - reportedly cutting herbicide use by up to ~98%.

name: ARA
desc: The Ecorobotix ARA is an ultra-high-precision smart sprayer with six cameras and 156 nozzles achieving ~6x6 cm spray resolution, applying plant-by-plant microdoses and cutting chemical use by 70-95%. Tractor-towed, with 20+ crop-specific AI algorithms.
use_cases: AI plant-by-plant precision spraying (6 m boom, ~6x6 cm targeting)

name: FD20
desc: The FarmDroid FD20 is a fully solar-powered autonomous robot that both seeds and mechanically weeds row crops. It records each seed's RTK-GPS position (8 mm) at sowing, so it can weed between and within rows before plants even emerge. ~1,250 kg (low soil compaction), 18-24 h/day CO2-neutral operation, ~6 ha/day, 50+ crop types; the +Spray option cuts chemicals up to 94%.

name: E-Series
desc: The Agrobot E-Series is an AI-vision strawberry-harvesting robot with up to 24 independent robotic arms that identify ripe berries and pick them with ~1 cm tolerance, avoiding unripe fruit and minimising bruising for premium markets.
actuator_type: Up to 24 independent picking arms with AI ripeness vision

name: Astronaut A5
desc: The Lely Astronaut A5 is an automatic (robotic) milking system that lets cows be milked voluntarily on demand; a robotic arm with 3D laser-guided teat detection attaches the cups while the system tracks per-cow yield and health data.

name: Origin
desc: The Cruise Origin (GM) was a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free shared robotaxi. Development was wound down after GM ended Cruise's robotaxi program in 2024 - included here as a notable discontinued milestone in the robotaxi category.
use_cases: Shared autonomous ride-hailing (program wound down 2024; design never mass-deployed)

name: Gen-7 Robotaxi
desc: Pony.ai's seventh-generation Robotaxi entered mass production in 2025 - the first to use 100% automotive-grade components with a ~70% lower autonomous-driving-kit BOM. Pony.ai runs fully-driverless service across China's four tier-one cities.
config: Built on GAC & BAIC platforms; automotive-grade
feature: ~70% lower autonomous-kit BOM vs prior gen
cameras: Multi-sensor kit: LiDAR + radar + cameras (100% automotive-grade)
use_cases: Driverless robotaxi (Toyota, GAC & BAIC vehicle platforms, mass production 2025)

name: Autonomous Shuttle (Sienna)
desc: May Mobility operates autonomous microtransit shuttles (Toyota Sienna platform) for on-demand and fixed-route public transit in several US cities, moving toward driver-out L4 operation in defined service zones.
use_cases: Public microtransit shuttle service (multi-passenger autonomous transit)

name: Aurora Driver (Autonomous Truck)
desc: The Aurora Driver is a self-driving system for Class 8 freight trucks; Aurora launched commercial driverless freight runs on Texas highways (Dallas-Houston) in 2025, hauling loads with no human in the cab.
use_cases: Driverless freight (Aurora Horizon subscription; launched commercial driverless 2025)

name: Kodiak Driver
desc: The Kodiak Driver is a self-driving system for long-haul and off-road trucking; Kodiak delivered driverless commercial trucks for customers (including Permian Basin oilfield routes) and focuses on autonomous freight at scale.
use_cases: Driverless freight hauling (vehicle-agnostic, 2.5M+ test miles; Bosch manufacturing partnership)

name: Mission Master SP
desc: The Rheinmetall Mission Master SP is a wheeled autonomous UGV optimised for stealth, modularity and network integration, used for reconnaissance, light resupply and close support to infantry, with swappable mission modules (cargo, surveillance, CASEVAC).

name: Titan
desc: Titan (QinetiQ North America with Milrem) is a modular tracked UGV providing "lighten-the-load" support for dismounted units - a reconfigurable platform that mounts different superstructures for transport, reconnaissance and rescue missions.

name: Optio-X20
desc: The KNDS/Nexter Optio-X20 is a tracked robotic combat platform (and the Ultro-600 robotic mule sibling) evaluated by European armies for logistics and armed support roles, carrying up to ~600 kg.
use_cases: Remote weapon platform, ISR, cargo (20-tonne class tracked UGV)

name: Ripsaw M5
desc: The Textron Ripsaw M5 is a tracked Robotic Combat Vehicle developed for the US Army RCV program, a high-mobility uncrewed platform designed to carry sensors, weapons and other payloads ahead of crewed formations.
use_cases: Robotic combat vehicle (US Army RCV-M candidate)

name: Gereon RCS
desc: The ARX Robotics Gereon RCS is a lightweight tracked UGV for European armed forces, used for logistics, reconnaissance and as a mobile sensor/effector carrier; designed for scalable, software-defined autonomy.
use_cases: Logistics, casualty evacuation, ISR (scalable modular platform)

name: TRX (Tracked Robot 10-ton)
desc: The General Dynamics TRX is a hybrid-electric tracked uncrewed platform (evolved from the MUTT family) configurable for logistics, breaching, counter-UAS, indirect fire and other payloads in support of mechanised formations.
payload: Payload capacity ~equal to vehicle weight (10-ton class)

name: PROBOT
desc: The Roboteam PROBOT is a compact wheeled logistics UGV that carries up to ~750 kg of supplies or casualties for dismounted units, with autonomous follow-me and waypoint navigation.
use_cases: Cargo transport (up to 750 kg), casualty evac, ISR

name: Skypod
desc: The Exotec Skypod is a goods-to-person warehouse robot that drives on the floor and climbs storage racks up to ~12 m to retrieve bins, combining high-density storage with fast picking. Travels ~4 m/s; deployed by major retailers and 3PLs worldwide.
use_cases: Goods-to-person warehouse fulfillment (climbs racks to 12 m)

name: HaiPick A42
desc: The Hai Robotics HaiPick A42 is an autonomous case-handling robot that retrieves multiple totes/cartons from high racks (up to ~10 m) and delivers them to pick stations, pioneering the ACR category for dense, flexible warehouse storage.

name: Ranger
desc: The GreyOrange Ranger family are goods-to-person and sortation AMRs that move racks or totes to operators, orchestrated by GreyOrange's GreyMatter fulfilment software for retail and e-commerce warehouses.
use_cases: Warehouse goods-to-person & sortation AMR fleet (GreyMatter software)

name: Palion Tow Tractor
desc: The Seegrid Palion Tow Tractor is a vision-guided (camera-based, infrastructure-free) autonomous tow tractor for material movement in manufacturing and warehousing, part of Seegrid's Palion line alongside pallet trucks and lift trucks.

name: Palion Pallet Truck (RPL)
desc: Vecna Robotics builds autonomous pallet trucks and tuggers for warehouse material handling, with the Pivotal orchestration platform and a human-in-the-loop remote support model for handling edge cases.

name: MiR1200 Pallet Jack
desc: The MiR1200 Pallet Jack (Mobile Industrial Robots, a Teradyne company) uses AI-powered 3D vision to autonomously locate, pick and deliver pallets, carrying up to ~1,200 kg - extending the MiR AMR line into pallet handling.

name: Pegasus
desc: Amazon Robotics Pegasus is a compact drive unit with a conveyor top that carries individual packages across a sortation floor and tips them into the correct chute, improving package-sorting accuracy in Amazon fulfilment centres.
actuator_type: Drive unit with conveyor top module
use_cases: Package sortation in Amazon fulfillment centers

name: FoxBot
desc: The Fox Robotics FoxBot is an autonomous trailer-unloading forklift that automatically unloads palletised freight from trucks at the dock, addressing one of the most labour-intensive and injury-prone warehouse tasks.
use_cases: Autonomous trailer unloading & dock work (robotic forklift)

name: inVia Picker
desc: The inVia Picker is a goods-to-person robot that autonomously retrieves totes from standard shelving and brings them to pick stations, offered under a robotics-as-a-service model for e-commerce fulfilment.

name: da Vinci 5
desc: The Intuitive da Vinci 5 (FDA-cleared March 2024) is the fifth-generation multiport robotic-assisted surgery system, adding first-of-its-kind Force Feedback, a new 3D display and 150+ enhancements over da Vinci Xi. Used across most surgical specialties; going international through 2025.
key_feature: Force Feedback technology; ~10,000x compute of da Vinci Xi
actuator_type: Force-feedback instrument arms (first in da Vinci line)

name: Ottava
desc: Ottava is Johnson & Johnson MedTech's soft-tissue surgical robot, uniquely integrating four arms into the operating table for a low profile and flexible setup. First US clinical cases (incl. gastric bypass) were completed in 2025, with an FDA submission expected in early 2026.
approach: Four arms integrated into the OR table
regulatory: Investigational - first US clinical cases done; FDA submission expected early 2026
use_cases: Multi-specialty soft-tissue surgery (6 arms integrated into the OR table; clinical trials underway)

name: Maestro
desc: The Moon Surgical Maestro is an accessible surgical-assistance robot that works with standard laparoscopic instruments, adding two robotic arms to hold and position the camera and tools - designed to fit existing OR workflows affordably. FDA-cleared and CE-marked.
key_feature: Two assistive arms that fit existing OR workflow
use_cases: Collaborative laparoscopic surgery (works with existing instruments; FDA-cleared & CE-marked)

name: Mazor X Stealth
desc: The Medtronic Mazor X Stealth Edition is a spine surgical robot combining preoperative planning with robotic guidance and integrated navigation for precise pedicle-screw and implant placement.
use_cases: Robotic-guided spine surgery with StealthStation navigation & predictive analytics

name: Senhance
desc: The Asensus Senhance is a digital laparoscopic surgical system with reusable instruments, haptic force feedback and eye-tracking camera control, aiming to lower per-procedure cost while adding digital intelligence to surgery.
key_feature: Haptic force feedback + eye-tracking camera control
use_cases: Digital laparoscopic surgery with reusable instruments

name: CORI
desc: The Smith+Nephew CORI Surgical System is a compact handheld robotic platform for partial and total knee replacement, using real-time bone mapping (no preoperative CT) and a robotics-assisted bur for precise resurfacing.

name: CyberKnife S7
desc: The Accuray CyberKnife S7 mounts a linear accelerator on a robotic arm to deliver highly targeted radiation to tumours from many angles, with real-time motion tracking that adjusts for patient and tumour movement.
actuator_type: Robotic manipulator with linear accelerator, real-time motion tracking (Synchrony)

name: Monarch Platform
desc: The Monarch Platform (J&J MedTech, originally Auris Health) is a robotic flexible-endoscopy system using a controller-driven scope for peripheral lung biopsy (bronchoscopy) and kidney-stone removal (urology), with navigation guidance.

name: PUDU T300
desc: The PUDU T300 is an industrial-grade autonomous delivery robot for factories and warehouses, carrying heavy loads with high precision and integrating with lifts and automatic doors for end-to-end material flow.

name: PUDU CC1 Pro
desc: The PUDU CC1 Pro is an AI-powered four-in-one commercial cleaning robot - sweeping, scrubbing, vacuuming and dust-mopping - with AI-driven perception and decision-making for offices, malls and transport hubs.
use_cases: Multi-mode commercial floor cleaning: sweep, scrub, vacuum, mop

name: HolaBot
desc: The Pudu HolaBot is a heavy-load (~60 kg) delivery and bussing robot with large enclosed shelves, used for food running and dish return in busy restaurants; summoned via call bells and capable of dish-collection cycles.

name: KLEENBOT C30
desc: The KEENON KLEENBOT C30 is a commercial floor-cleaning robot combining sweeping, scrubbing and drying with autonomous navigation for malls, airports and offices.
use_cases: Commercial floor cleaning (sweep, vacuum, dust mop — 61 cm width, 19,000 Pa suction, 2,500 m² per charge)

name: Whiz
desc: The SoftBank Whiz is an autonomous commercial vacuum-sweeping robot (BrainOS-powered) for offices, hotels and retail, learning routes by being driven once then repeating them autonomously; SoftBank's flagship after refocusing from the Pepper humanoid.
use_cases: Commercial vacuum cleaning (up to 1,500 m² per charge)

name: Neo
desc: The Avidbots Neo is a fully-autonomous floor-scrubbing robot for large commercial spaces (airports, malls, warehouses), self-navigating and self-cleaning with detailed cleaning reports; the Neo 2 added improved autonomy and analytics.

name: T7AMR
desc: The Tennant T7AMR is a robotic floor-scrubbing machine (BrainOS-powered) that autonomously scrubs hard floors in retail, warehouse and institutional settings while still usable as a manual ride/walk-behind scrubber.

name: K5
desc: The Knightscope K5 is a large autonomous outdoor security robot that patrols parking lots, campuses and malls, streaming 360° video, reading licence plates and detecting anomalies, offered on a Robot-as-a-Service subscription.

name: CLOi ServeBot
desc: The LG CLOi ServeBot is an autonomous serving/delivery robot with multiple shelves for restaurants, hotels and hospitals, part of LG's CLOi commercial-robot line (alongside GuideBot and CleanBot).

name: Gen3 Delivery Robot
desc: The Serve Robotics third-generation sidewalk delivery robot (spun out of Uber) runs Level 4 autonomy on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin brain with Ouster LiDAR, ~11 mph top speed, ~14 h battery and ~15 gal insulated cargo (holds 4x 16" pizzas).
