Serve deployed its 2,000th robot in 2025 across LA, Miami, Dallas, Chicago and Atlanta with Uber Eats and DoorDash.

name: Coco Bot
desc: Coco operates pink insulated sidewalk delivery robots for restaurant orders, using a remote-piloted-plus-autonomy model for safe urban navigation; widely deployed in Los Angeles and other US cities.

name: Delivery Robot
desc: Avride (spun out of Yandex's self-driving group) builds six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery robots deployed with Uber Eats and Grubhub, alongside its autonomous-vehicle work; operates in several US cities.

name: Ottobot Yeti
desc: The Ottonomy Ottobot is a fully-autonomous delivery robot used both indoors (airports, retail) and outdoors (curbside, sidewalk), with contextual-AI navigation and multi-compartment cargo for parcels, food and pharmacy.

name: Neolix Delivery Vehicle
desc: Neolix builds compact driverless delivery vans for last-mile logistics, retail-on-wheels and contactless delivery, deployed at scale across Chinese cities for parcel and grocery distribution.
use_cases: Level-4 urban unmanned delivery vehicle (retail, logistics, vending)

name: Ingenuity
desc: Ingenuity was NASA/JPL's Mars helicopter - the first powered, controlled flight on another planet (Apr 2021). Just 1.8 kg with counter-rotating rotors and solar charging, it flew 72 times over ~3 years (vs a 5-flight plan), covering ~17 km, before rotor-blade damage grounded it in Jan 2024.
achievement: First powered, controlled flight on another planet

name: Nova-C (Odysseus)
desc: The Intuitive Machines Nova-C "Odysseus" was the first US lunar lander since Apollo and the first commercial soft landing on the Moon (IM-1, Feb 2024). A ~1,900 kg hexagonal-cylinder lander (100 kg payload) that touched down near the lunar south pole, tipping on landing but returning data.
achievement: First US lunar landing since Apollo; first commercial soft landing

name: Astrobee
desc: Astrobee is NASA's system of cube-shaped free-flying robots (Bumble, Honey, Queen) aboard the ISS, using electric impeller fans to fly weightlessly and cameras/sensors to navigate the Kibo module - assisting astronauts and hosting student programming challenges.

name: SORA-Q (LEV-2)
desc: SORA-Q (LEV-2) is JAXA's baseball-sized (~250 g) transformable lunar rover deployed by the SLIM "Moon Sniper" lander (Jan 2024). It splits open into a two-wheeled crawler to image the lander and terrain - co-developed with toy maker Tomy, Sony and Doshisha University.

name: CADRE Rovers
desc: CADRE (Cooperative Autonomous Distributed Robotic Explorers) is a set of small shoebox-sized NASA rovers designed to operate together autonomously as a team on the Moon, demonstrating multi-robot coordination; manifested on the IM-3 mission.
objective: Autonomous multi-robot coordination on the Moon
use_cases: Cooperative multi-robot lunar exploration (3 autonomous shoebox-sized rovers mapping in formation; Intuitive Machines IM-3 delivery)

name: CIMON
desc: CIMON (Crew Interactive Mobile Companion) is a free-floating, AI-powered spherical assistant aboard the ISS, built by Airbus for DLR with IBM Watson voice AI - it talks with astronauts, displays procedures and floats via internal fans.
cameras: Front camera + microphones for crew interaction

name: Canadarm3
desc: Canadarm3 is Canada's AI-enabled robotic system for NASA's Lunar Gateway - a smart, largely autonomous arm (built by MDA) that will maintain, repair and inspect the Gateway station in lunar orbit without constant human control.

name: European Robotic Arm (ERA)
desc: The European Robotic Arm (ERA) is a ~11 m symmetrical robotic arm on the ISS Russian segment that can "walk" end-over-end between fixed base points to move payloads and assist spacewalks; built by Airbus for ESA.

name: VEX IQ
desc: VEX IQ is a snap-together plastic robotics platform for elementary and middle school, central to the VEX IQ competition; programmable in VEXcode (blocks or Python) and widely adopted in school robotics leagues.

name: VEX GO
desc: VEX GO is an affordable elementary STEM kit with colourful snap-together parts, a code-able brain, motors and sensors, designed for hands-on early-grades robotics and engineering lessons.

name: mBot2
desc: The Makeblock mBot2 is an upgraded entry-level coding robot built on the CyberPi controller with Wi-Fi, supporting Scratch and Python; popular as a school class-pack for line-following, obstacle avoidance and AIoT projects.

name: mBot Ranger
desc: The Makeblock mBot Ranger is a 3-in-1 transformable robotics kit (tank, self-balancing car, three-wheel racer) with block-based mBlock and Arduino programming for intermediate STEM learners.
use_cases: 3-in-1 STEM build: tank / three-wheel racer / self-balancing robot

name: Cue
desc: Wonder Workshop Cue is an upgraded sibling of Dash for older students, with witty AI "avatars", text/block coding and JavaScript support to bridge from beginner to more advanced programming.

name: JIMU Robot
desc: UBTECH JIMU Robot kits (e.g. AstroBot, BuilderBots) are snap-together robotic building sets with servos, sensors and a controller, programmed via the Blockly-based app to build and animate creations - blending construction play with coding.

name: ROSMASTER X3
desc: The Yahboom ROSMASTER X3 is an advanced education robot supporting ROS2, SLAM, LiDAR and machine-learning modules on a mecanum-wheel base - a testbed bridging classroom STEM and real robotics research/Jetson development.
cpu: NVIDIA Jetson Nano / Orin NX options

name: T1
desc: The Booster Robotics T1 is a compact (~1.2 m, ~30 kg) research/education humanoid with 23-41 DOF and a fall-resilient design. The championship model of the 2025 RoboCup "AdultSize" soccer league, used by 50+ top robotics teams and institutes; developer-friendly SDK.

name: CL-1
desc: The LimX Dynamics CL-1 is a full-size (~1.65 m) general-purpose humanoid notable for real-time terrain perception and dynamic stair climbing, developed alongside LimX's TRON 1 point-foot biped as a robot-learning platform.
feature: Real-time terrain perception; dynamic stair climbing
actuator_type: Hollow direct-drive motors, dynamic whole-body control
use_cases: Research demonstrator: dynamic stair climbing, heavy-load handling (succeeded by LimX Oli; detailed specs never published)

name: DR01 (Dr.01)
desc: The DEEP Robotics DR01 is the quadruped specialist's first full-size humanoid, demonstrating stable dynamic walking and running; it extends DEEP Robotics' locomotion expertise from legged dogs to bipeds.
actuator_type: Proprietary J60 lightweight + J100 high-torque joints

name: Adam
desc: PNDbotics Adam is a full-size (~1.6 m) humanoid with a high degree-of-freedom body and expressive motion, shown performing music and dance demos and targeted at research and interactive applications.
cpu: Intel i7 NUC + PND real-time control unit
sdk: Open-source SDK, NVIDIA Isaac Gym DRL training

name: PM01
desc: EngineAI’s lightweight open humanoid platform (CES 2025). At 1.38 m and 40 kg with 24 DoF and 320° waist rotation, the PM01 pairs an Intel N97 with NVIDIA Jetson Orin and ships fully open-source (ROS/ONNX, MuJoCo, Isaac) for developers. Founded by Zhao Tongyang, former lead of XPENG’s humanoid program.
actuator_type: Custom electric actuators, self-developed joint modules, dual encoders
cpu: Dual compute: Intel N97 (x86) + NVIDIA Jetson Orin
cameras: Intel RealSense D435i depth camera + multi-array microphones
sdk: Open-source: ROS/ONNX, MuJoCo sim2sim, Isaac training

name: SE01
desc: EngineAI’s flagship full-size humanoid, unveiled October 2024 — claimed as the first humanoid to achieve a natural human-like gait via an end-to-end neural network. At 170 cm and 55 kg with 32 DoF, it uses self-developed harmonic/planetary/ball-screw joints rated to 186 N·m, an aerospace-aluminum 10-year frame, and quick-swap batteries. Founded by Zhao Tongyang (ex-XPENG PX5 lead).
perception: Engine Sense 360 deg LiDAR + depth camera
actuator_type: Self-developed harmonic, planetary & ball-screw joints; dual encoders; cross-roller bearings; forced-air joint cooling
use_cases: Commercial & educational (CCTV New Year Gala debut)
cameras: Depth camera + multi-mic array + LiDAR 360° (Engine Sense)
ai_model: End-to-end neural network (RL + imitation learning) — first humanoid with natural human-like gait

name: MagicBot Z1
desc: MagicLab's MagicBot (Z1) is a full-size humanoid built for industrial and commercial tasks, shown handling tools and demonstrating dexterous manipulation; part of China's rapidly growing humanoid cohort.
hand_type: Optional MagicHand S01 dexterous hand (11 DoF, tactile)
use_cases: Industrial, commercial & research humanoid (expandable to 50 DoF)

name: Isaac
desc: Isaac (Weave Robotics) is a home-focused humanoid designed for household chores like tidying and laundry, combining autonomy with teleoperated assistance and a subscription model; pre-orders opened in 2024-2025 for a 2026 launch.
use_cases: Home chores: laundry folding, tidying (preorder, 2026 deliveries)

name: A1
desc: Galaxea AI's A1 is a high-precision robotic arm/manipulation platform, part of Galaxea's lineup (with the R1 wheeled humanoid) targeting embodied-AI data collection and general manipulation.
use_cases: Robotic manipulation & embodied-AI research platform (mobile + tabletop variants)

name: GoMate
desc: GoMate is automaker GAC's humanoid robot featuring a variable wheeled-leg system (switching between two-wheel and four-wheel modes), intended for automotive-plant logistics and eventually consumer applications.

name: Platform 2 (P2 Zip)
desc: Zipline's Platform 2 (P2 Zip) is an autonomous delivery drone that hovers and lowers a tethered "droid" on a line to place packages precisely on doorsteps, extending Zipline's long-range medical/retail delivery network to homes.
actuator_type: Hybrid VTOL fixed-wing + tethered delivery droid

name: Wing Delivery Drone
desc: Wing (an Alphabet company) operates fixed-wing/multirotor hybrid autonomous delivery drones that carry small packages from local hubs to homes, with commercial operations in the US, Australia and beyond.

name: CRX-25iA
desc: The FANUC CRX-25iA is a high-payload (25 kg) addition to the CRX collaborative line with a long ~1,889 mm reach, aimed at palletizing and heavier machine-tending, using the same controller/programming as FANUC's industrial robots.

name: TM30
desc: The Techman TM30 is a high reach-to-payload cobot (35 kg payload, 1,702 mm reach) with built-in AI Vision, ideal for palletizing and semiconductor back-end tasks like lifting heavy wafer boxes.

name: TM25S
desc: The Techman TM25S is a 25 kg-payload cobot with integrated vision and software for digital twins, visual inspection, welding and palletizing - extending Techman's vision-standard approach to heavier tasks.

name: GoFa 12
desc: The ABB GoFa 12 is a higher-payload (12 kg) member of ABB's GoFa collaborative family, designed for material handling, machine tending and palletizing alongside human workers without safety fencing in many applications.

name: E0509 (E-Series)
desc: The Doosan E0509 is a lightweight, food-grade cobot in Doosan's E-Series (5 kg payload, 900 mm reach) with a hygienic design for food handling and light assembly, part of Doosan's A/M/H/E lineup.

name: AquaSense 2 Ultra
desc: The Beatbot AquaSense 2 Ultra (CES 2025 flagship) is a cordless robotic pool cleaner covering floor, walls, waterline and water surface. AI HybridSense navigation (27 sensors incl. cameras + ultrasonics) builds a pool map and targets high-debris zones; dual brushes, a 5 L debris basket (150um+250um dual filter), dual LED night cleaning and self-parking at the pool edge. ~3.5 h runtime, 4-5 h charge.

name: Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus
desc: The Maytronics Dolphin Nautilus CC Plus is a popular corded robotic pool cleaner (~8.6 kg) with dual scrubbing brushes, a large top-load filter, wall-climbing and CleverClean navigation, plus app scheduling on the CC Plus model. 60 ft anti-tangle swivel cable for in-ground pools.

name: S2 Solar
desc: The WYBOT S2 Solar is a solar-powered autonomous surface pool skimmer that floats and continuously collects leaves and debris from the water surface, recharging from the sun for hands-free daily skimming.
battery_type: Rechargeable, with floating solar charging dock

name: HOBOT-S6
desc: The HOBOT-S6 is a window-cleaning robot using ultrasonic water spray and a tri-spray system with AI route planning, cleaning framed and frameless glass with a safety tether and battery backup against power loss.

name: Litter-Robot 4
desc: The Whisker Litter-Robot 4 is a self-cleaning automatic litter box that sifts and rotates to separate waste after each use, with OmniSense weight/litter-level sensing that tracks each cat's weight and litter level, reporting to the Whisker app over Wi-Fi.

name: Grillbot
desc: Grillbot is an automatic grill-cleaning robot with three motorised brushes and a CPU-timed cleaning cycle that scrubs barbecue grates hands-free while the grill is warm.

name: Tertill
desc: Tertill (Franklin Robotics) is a solar-powered weeding robot that lives in a garden bed year-round, patrolling daily and using a string trimmer to cut down small weeds while sensing and avoiding established plants.

name: Ghost (Anduril sUAS)
desc: The Anduril Ghost is a modular autonomous small unmanned aircraft system for reconnaissance and ISR, powered by Anduril's Lattice AI for autonomous mission execution; used by defense and security customers. (Distinct from Ghost Robotics quadrupeds.)

name: Ion Endoluminal (Bronchoscopy)
desc: The Intuitive Ion is a robotic endoluminal platform for minimally invasive peripheral lung biopsy, using an ultrathin, maneuverable shape-sensing catheter to navigate deep into the lung for early cancer diagnosis.
use_cases: Robotic bronchoscopy for peripheral lung biopsy

name: 8R Autonomous (driverless kit)
desc: John Deere's autonomous 8R adds a retrofit autonomy kit (six stereo camera pairs, GPS and onboard AI) to its 8R tractor line, enabling driver-free tillage and field work with remote monitoring and control via a mobile dashboard.
sensing: 6 stereo camera pairs + GPS + onboard AI

name: Guardian XO (full-body exoskeleton)
desc: A full-body powered exoskeleton letting a worker lift up to 90 kg as if a fraction of the weight, at ~200:1 amplification. The 24-DoF Guardian XO runs on hot-swappable batteries for continuous shift work.
use_cases: Industrial heavy lifting — logistics, aviation, defense

name: T800
desc: The EngineAI T800 is the company's flagship full-size humanoid (CES 2026 debut, mass production from ~June 2026): ~1.73 m, ~75 kg, 29 body DOF (+7/hand), up to 3 m/s, 450 Nm peak-torque joints, a magnesium-aluminium alloy frame and a notable solid-state battery (~3 h). NVIDIA Jetson compute, 360 deg LiDAR + RealSense. Went viral for fluid martial-arts demos; offered in multiple editions from ~5,000.

name: HMND 01 (Alpha Bipedal)
desc: HMND 01 is London-based startup Humanoid's first bipedal robot - a ~1.79 m general-purpose humanoid with 29 DOF and ~15 kg bimanual payload that achieved stable walking just 48 hours after final assembly (design-to-prototype in five months). Working with Bosch to scale production; 19,000+ pre-orders reported.
use_cases: Labor automation humanoid (UK; announced target specs)

name: Reachy Mini
desc: Reachy Mini (Hugging Face, from Pollen Robotics) is a low-cost open-source expressive desktop robot for embodied-AI development - a moving/animated head with camera, mics and speaker, programmable in Python and integrated with the Hugging Face Hub. A May 2026 agentic toolkit lets users build working apps in under an hour with no manual coding. Lite (~99) and wireless (~49) versions.
sdk: Open-source Python SDK, Hugging Face Hub integration

name: Oli
ai: LimX embodied AI stack — COSA, VGM, DreamActor, Agentic OS
desc: Oli is LimX Dynamics' full-size general-purpose humanoid for research, manufacturing and commercial use — 165 cm (Super tier 175 cm), ≤55 kg, with 31 active DoF (6/leg, 7/arm, 3 waist, 2 neck), up to 43 on the top tier. Unlike the performance-focused Luna, Oli is a developer platform: head/chest/hip depth cameras, LiDAR, an in-house IMU and interchangeable end-effectors up to a 6-DoF five-finger hand. Compute pairs an RK3588 controller with an NVIDIA Orin NX (157 TOPS), expandable to a 275-TOPS AGX Orin backpack, with a full SDK and low/high-level motion APIs. Sold as Lite, EDU and Super tiers.
dof_breakdown: Legs 6×2, Arms 7×2, Waist 3, Neck 2 (31; up to 43 on Super tier)
battery: 9,500 mAh; ~2 h (Lite/EDU), ~1.5 h (Super); charger 58.8V/10A; drawer-type module
end_effector: Parallel two-finger gripper (1 DoF) standard; optional five-finger dexterous hand (6 DoF), self-developed two-finger (1 DoF) or three-finger dexterous hand (4 DoF)
controller: Handheld remote; optional handheld emergency stop
compute: Remote control RK3588 (8-16G); Perception NVIDIA Orin NX 157TOPS (EDU/Super); optional computing backpack AGX Orin 275TOPS
connectivity: Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, USB 3.0/3.2, Gigabit Ethernet, Type-C, 5G (higher tiers)
software: Secondary development; controller & sensor APIs; low- & high-level motion-control APIs (walking, mobile manipulation, teleoperation); OTA; Studio package; voice, light interaction, status monitoring, basic motion library
depth_sensing: Head, chest & hip depth cameras + wrist mount

name: TRON 1
compute: 12th Gen Intel i3 / 16GB / 512GB; operating range -5°C to 40°C
feature: 3-in-1 modular foot-ends — Point-Foot, Sole, Wheeled; climbs ≤30°; clears ≤20 cm obstacles
software: SDK, data visualization, record & playback, joint-control algorithms, simulation platform; secondary development; OTA
desc: TRON 1 is billed as the first multi-modal biped robot — a compact (≤845 mm, ≤20 kg) all-terrain research and RL platform with interchangeable Point-Foot, Sole and Wheeled foot-ends. It carries up to 10 kg, climbs 30°, clears 20 cm obstacles, and runs ~2 h on a 46.8V/4.5Ah quick-swap pack. 48V actuators deliver 30 N·m rated / 60 N·m peak at 15 rad/s; a 12th-gen Intel i3 brain, IMU (optional RGBD) and an open SDK with simulation tooling make it a favourite locomotion/RL testbed. Standard and EDU editions.
max_speed: Point-foot <1 m/s, Sole <1 m/s, Wheeled ≤3 m/s
actuators: 48V; rated torque 30 N·m, peak 60 N·m; peak speed 15 rad/s
battery: 46.8V ternary lithium, 4.5 Ah, 1,000 W max; ≤2 h; quick-swap; <1 h (20-80%) / 1.5 h full
connectivity: USB 3.0 ×1, Gigabit Ethernet ×1; 24V/100W (peak 200W) peripheral power; peripheral mounting points
controller: Handheld remote (50 m range) with E-stop
actuator_type: 48V joint actuators — 30 N·m rated, 60 N·m peak, 15 rad/s

name: TRON 2
feature: Multi-form embodied robot platform; successor to TRON 1 in LimX's layered lineup
desc: TRON 2 is LimX Dynamics' multi-form embodied robot — one body, three configurations — pairing high-performance dual 7-DoF manipulator arms with all-terrain bipedal/wheeled mobility for VLA research, mobile manipulation and whole-body control. Each arm lifts up to 5 kg at 5 m/s with ±0.5 mm repeatability and Quest 3 VR teleoperation (100 ms delay); the base does up to 5 m/s on wheels, climbs 30°, and carries 30 kg on flat ground. Powered by a 46.8V/9Ah swappable pack (30-min fast charge), sensed by waist/head/wrist RGBD cameras and an IMU, driven by an Intel i7 AI computing box with full SDK, ROS1/ROS2 and simulation tooling. EDU and Standard editions.
dual_arm: Max 5 kg/arm (3 kg extended); end-effector speed 5 m/s, accel 36 m/s²; repeat accuracy ±0.5 mm; VR teleop (Oculus Quest 3), 100 ms delay; gripper (20 N, 85 mm) or dexterous hand
mobility: Multi-form base — Sole 2-3 m/s / Wheeled 3-5 m/s; climbs 15° (sole) / 30° (wheeled); 20 cm step; load 30 kg flat-ground, 20 kg stair-climbing
battery: 46.8V ternary lithium, 9 Ah, 2,800 W max; charge 542 W, 30 min (20-80%) / 54 min (100%); swappable
connectivity: Ethernet, USB 3.0, EtherCAT ×2, RS485; 12V/24V/48V power outputs
compute: AI computing box — Intel Core i7-1165G7, 2TB; 4×ETH, 4×USB 3.0
software: SDK, robot management / data / simulation platforms; Python, C++, ROS1/ROS2

name: P1
feature: Point-foot bipedal locomotion; RL testbed; robust untethered walking across unstructured outdoor terrain (grass, slopes, woodland)
desc: P1 is LimX Dynamics' point-foot bipedal robot, known for reinforcement-learning demonstrations of robust untethered walking over rough outdoor terrain. It was the base from which LimX developed the motion-control algorithms behind its CL-1 humanoid, and a predecessor to the TRON modular biped line.

name: Luna
battery: Drawer-style hot-swap module; direct charge or hot-swap; ~1 h charge; 110-220V in, 58.8V/10A out
end_effector: Palm-shaped hand (standard); optional fist-shaped or dexterous 5-finger hand (6 DoF)
interaction: Face interaction screen, microphone, speaker, LED indicator strip
features: OTA, app, optional custom skin, portable carrying case, content development kit (tablet + software: video imitation, manual teaching, choreography, smart tasks, swarm control)
desc: Luna is LimX Dynamics' full-size interactive humanoid, built primarily for commercial performance in malls, attractions, trade shows and entertainment venues. It stands 160 cm (47 cm shoulder, 69 cm reach), weighs 54 kg, and has 27 active DoF, combining high-dynamic motion with multi-modal interaction. A 10,000 mAh drawer-style hot-swap battery gives ~4 h; dual RK3588 compute drives motion and perception; and a face interaction screen, speaker, mic and LED strip — plus optional custom skin and a content-development kit (choreography, swarm control, video imitation) — make it a turnkey performance robot.

name: N1
sdk: Fully open-source: BOM, CAD drawings, assembly SOP & control software on GitHub
use_cases: 1,000+ hours outdoor-tested: slopes, stairs, fall recovery
desc: China’s first fully open-source, engineering-verified humanoid robot. 1,000+ hours of outdoor testing: 15–20° slopes, 20 cm stairs, fall recovery.

name: Elektro
desc: The celebrity robot of the 1939 New York World’s Fair. Elektro walked by voice command, spoke ~700 words via 78-rpm records, distinguished colors with photoelectric eyes — and famously smoked cigarettes. Joined by robot dog Sparko in 1940. The earliest surviving American humanoid icon.
actuator_type: Electric motors, relay logic, photoelectric sensors

name: Elmer & Elsie (Tortoises)
desc: Machina Speculatrix — the first autonomous electronic robots. Built by neurophysiologist W. Grey Walter in Bristol, these phototropic "tortoises" sought light, avoided obstacles and returned to their hutch to recharge, exhibiting lifelike behavior from just two vacuum-tube "neurons".
actuator_type: Two vacuum-tube analog control, photocell steering, drive + steer motors

name: Theseus
desc: Claude Shannon’s maze-solving mechanical mouse — one of the first machine-learning devices ever built. Theseus explored a 25-square maze by trial and error, then "remembered" the solution using telephone relay circuits under the maze floor.
actuator_type: Electromagnet drive under maze floor, relay-circuit memory

name: Unimate
desc: The first industrial robot in history. Born from George Devol’s 1954 patent and Joseph Engelberger’s vision, Unimate went to work on a General Motors die-casting line in Trenton, New Jersey in 1961 — unloading hot metal parts no human wanted to touch. It launched the entire robotics industry.
use_cases: Die-casting handling & spot welding (GM production lines)

name: Shakey
desc: The first mobile robot that could reason about its own actions (1966–72). Shakey perceived its world with a TV camera and bump sensors, planned with the STRIPS algorithm, and rerouted around obstacles — work that produced A* search, computer vision foundations and modern AI planning.
actuator_type: Wheeled base, radio link to SDS-940 mainframe

name: WABOT-1
desc: The world’s first full-scale anthropomorphic robot, built by Ichiro Kato’s lab at Waseda University. WABOT-1 walked on two legs, gripped with tactile hands, measured distances with artificial eyes and ears, and conversed in Japanese — with the estimated faculties of an 18-month-old child.
actuator_type: Hydraulic & electric limb control, tactile-sensor hands

name: WABOT-2
desc: Waseda’s musician humanoid — WABOT-2 read sheet music with its camera eye and played a keyboard organ with five-fingered hands and feet on the pedals, even accompanying singers. A landmark in dexterous manipulation and task specialization.

name: Stanford Cart
desc: A pioneering self-driving vehicle research platform. In its famous 1979 run under Hans Moravec, the Cart crossed a chair-filled room entirely autonomously in about five hours, using stereo TV vision processed by a remote mainframe — ancestral DNA of every modern autonomous vehicle.
use_cases: Early autonomous navigation & computer vision research

name: PUMA 560
desc: The Programmable Universal Machine for Assembly — Vic Scheinman’s elegant 6-axis electric arm became the most influential robot arm ever made, the de facto research standard for decades, and in 1985 performed the first robot-assisted surgery (a brain biopsy).

name: Skilam (first SCARA)
desc: The first commercial SCARA robot. Hiroshi Makino’s Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm concept (1978, Yamanashi University) reached factories in 1981 — rigid vertically, compliant horizontally, perfect for pick-and-place. SCARA remains a dominant assembly architecture today.

name: HERO 1
desc: The robot that taught a generation: Heathkit’s HERO 1 kit brought a Motorola 6808-powered robot with sonar ranging, light/sound sensors, speech synthesis and an optional arm into thousands of homes, schools and labs in the early-80s personal robot boom.
actuator_type: Wheeled base, optional gripper arm, speech synthesizer

name: RB5X
desc: One of the first mass-produced personal robots, from Golden, Colorado. The transparent-domed RB5X featured sonar, bump sensors, an optional arm and voice, and could "learn" from its environment — sold to homes and schools at the height of the 1980s robot craze.

name: Armatron
desc: The legendary toy robot arm. Armatron’s twin joysticks commanded a 6-movement gripper arm through an ingenious all-mechanical gearbox driven by a single motor — a masterpiece of mechanism design that inspired countless future engineers.
actuator_type: Single motor + mechanical transmission, dual-joystick control

name: Omnibot
desc: Tomy’s flagship 1980s home robot: programmable via its built-in cassette deck, remote-controlled, with a serving tray, digital clock and speech playback. The Omnibot line defined the era’s dream of the household robot butler.

name: Genghis
desc: Rodney Brooks’ six-legged insect robot that changed robotics philosophy: no world model, no central planner — just layered "subsumption architecture" behaviors that let a 1 kg machine scramble over rough terrain. Its DNA lives on in every behavior-based robot since.

name: Cog
desc: MIT’s upper-torso humanoid (1993–2003) built on the thesis that human-like intelligence requires a human-like body. Cog learned eye-hand coordination, object tracking and social cueing, seeding the embodied-AI movement and the humanoid wave that followed.
actuator_type: Upper-torso humanoid: head, trunk, two arms

name: Dante II
desc: The volcano explorer. In 1994 the eight-legged, tether-rappelling Dante II descended into Alaska’s active Mt. Spurr crater to sample fumarole gases too dangerous for humans — a foundational mission for extreme-environment and planetary robotics.

name: P2
desc: The December 1996 reveal that stunned the robotics world: Honda’s P2 was the first self-contained, wireless bipedal humanoid to walk with dynamic stability — climbing stairs and pushing carts with all computing and batteries onboard. The direct ancestor of ASIMO.
actuator_type: Electric servo bipedal locomotion, fully self-contained

name: P3
desc: Honda’s refinement of P2 — smaller, lighter (magnesium body), and the final stepping stone to ASIMO. P3 proved the miniaturization path that turned a 210 kg laboratory giant into a practical research humanoid.

name: Kismet
desc: Cynthia Breazeal’s expressive robot head — the founding work of social robotics. With ears, eyebrows, lips and eyes driven by 21 motors, Kismet read human tone and expression and responded with believable infant-like emotions, defining human-robot interaction as a field.

name: Furby
desc: The 40-million-selling animatronic phenomenon. Furby blinked, wiggled and "evolved" from Furbish to English using sensors for light, touch, sound and orientation — for millions of kids, the first robot they ever owned.

name: MINDSTORMS RCX
desc: The yellow brick that started it all: LEGO’s original MINDSTORMS programmable brick (developed with MIT Media Lab) put motors, sensors and code into classrooms worldwide and ignited the FIRST LEGO League generation of engineers.

name: AIBO ERS-110
desc: The first AIBO — Sony’s entertainment robot dog sold out its initial 3,000 Japanese units in 20 minutes in May 1999. With 18 joints, a camera nose and learned behaviors, ERS-110 created the consumer robot-companion category and remains a design icon.
cameras: Color CCD camera + range sensor + touch sensors

name: PaPeRo
desc: NEC’s Partner-type Personal Robot — a pioneering home social robot with face recognition for dozens of people, conversational speech, and childcare-assistant trials. PaPeRo’s research lineage shaped today’s companion-robot category.
cameras: Twin eye cameras with face recognition

name: QRIO
desc: Sony’s "Quest for cuRIOsity" — the first humanoid robot capable of running (officially certified by Guinness in 2005). The 58 cm QRIO walked, danced in troupes, threw balls, recognized faces and voices, and got up after falls; cancelled in 2006 alongside AIBO, never sold.

name: GD01
frame_material: High-strength alloy skeleton (titanium/aluminium elements, carbon fiber components)
actuator_type: Unitree high-torque motors; transforms between bipedal walking and quadrupedal crawl modes
use_cases: World’s first production-ready manned mecha (unveiled 12 May 2026)
Piloted civilian vehicle — open cockpit in torso
desc: The robot that broke the internet in May 2026: Unitree’s GD01 is the world’s first mass-produced manned mecha. A pilot sits in an open cockpit in the torso and drives a half-ton transforming machine that walks upright, drops to a four-legged crawl, and — in its launch video, piloted by CEO Wang Xingxing himself — punched its arm through a brick wall. From ~CN¥3.9 million (~US$650,000), with orders received on day one.

name: Archax
cameras: Cockpit monitor system fed by external cameras
actuator_type: 26 electrically actuated joints; transforms between upright robot mode and lowered vehicle mode (4 wheels)
use_cases: Pilotable luxury mecha (limited production run, ~US$2.7 million)
Inspired by Gundam — joystick + touch-panel cockpit controls
desc: Japan’s Gundam made real. Tsubame Industries’ Archax is a 4.5 m, 3.5-tonne rideable mecha with an enclosed cockpit: the pilot drives via joysticks and touch panels watching external camera feeds. It shifts from upright robot mode to a lowered wheeled vehicle mode. Built in a limited run for ultra-wealthy buyers at around US$2.7 million.

name: Eagle Prime (Mk.III)
actuator_type: 430 hp Chevrolet LS3 V8 driving hydraulics; tracked base; two-person cockpit (pilot + gunner)
use_cases: America’s entrant — and winner — of the 2017 USA-vs-Japan giant robot duel
Sports-entertainment combat mecha (paintball cannon, chainsaw, claw attachments)
desc: America’s 12-tonne answer to Kuratas. MegaBots’ Eagle Prime stood 4.9 m tall, ran a 430 hp V8, seated a two-person crew, and won the world’s first giant robot duel against Japan in October 2017 — chainsaw and all. After MegaBots wound down, Eagle Prime sold on eBay in 2021 for US$298,000, cementing its cult legend status.

name: Prosthesis
actuator_type: Pilot-amplifying exo-bionic control: the pilot’s arm movements drive the four legs directly — no autonomy, no software assistance
use_cases: The world’s first racing mech — built for a planned mech-racing league
Guinness World Record: largest tetrapod exoskeleton
desc: A 3.6-tonne electric racing animal. Prosthesis is pure pilot skill: your limbs drive its four giant legs through direct mechanical amplification — no AI, no balance software. Built by Furrion Exo-Bionics in Canada as the founding machine of a future mech-racing league, it holds the Guinness record for largest tetrapod exoskeleton and genuinely runs.

name: R1 Dual-Arm
ai_chip: Optional NVIDIA Jetson Orin module (boosts to 40-100 TOPS)
hand_type: Swappable end effectors: 2-, 3- and 5-finger dexterous hands
actuator_type: Upper-body dual-arm design on fixed base or mobile chassis; waist ±150°, head ±115°/±36°
sdk: Secondary development supported; UniStore app ecosystem
use_cases: Lowest-cost serious humanoid platform: from CN¥26,900 (~US$3,930)
desc: Unitree’s April 2026 disruptor: a dual-arm manipulation humanoid for under US$4,000. Arms configure to 5 or 7 DoF each (15-31 DoF total), grippers hit ±0.1 mm repeatability, and hands swap between 2-, 3- and 5-finger designs. Launched alongside Unitree’s first retail store on Beijing’s Wangfujing street — a humanoid you can walk in and buy.

name: Persona AI Humanoid
actuator_type: Rugged, heat-resistant design for welding, grinding & structural assembly
use_cases: Heavy fabrication in harsh, safety-critical environments
desc: Houston-based Persona AI is building a humanoid for one of the hardest jobs in industry: shipyard welding. Developed in partnership with HD Hyundai’s shipbuilding arm, the unnamed robot targets welding, grinding and structural assembly with rugged, heat-resistant construction — a working prototype is slated for late 2026.
